At the beginning of the term, Simona Mohamsson sat in the municipal council in Gothenburg and the social committee in Hisingen. She was a part-time politician, but the assignments were paid and provided a fee from the city.

In October 2022, Simona Mohamsson started an internship at the embassy in Amman, Jordan. After the internship, she got paid employment at the embassy. In total, she was in Amman for about a year. But she continued to collect the fee from Gothenburg.

TV4 Nyheterna has gone through Simona Mohamsson's meeting attendance for the political assignments in Gothenburg that she kept during her time at the embassy in Jordan. "Payments have taken place, despite high absenteeism" Between October 2022 and a year ahead, Simona Mohamsson attended two out of twelve meetings of the municipal council at home in Gothenburg. Of the 13 meetings the social committee held, she was present at three.

She participated remotely in a majority of so-called presidium meetings, a kind of planning meetings.

"Payments have been made, despite high absenteeism," asserts an official at the City of Gothenburg in a conversation with TV4 Nyheterna.

According to the city's regulations, it is the politicians themselves or their parties who must report absences or interruptions in the assignment - and that the payment of the fee must therefore be paused.

Simona Mohamsson says that the arrangement during the time she was in Jordan was agreed with both the social committee and L's group leader in Gothenburg.

- Ideally, I would have been able to go back and forth. It was not possible for me. This means that the risk of contracting TBE or Lyme disease is almost everywhere we spend time outdoors. TBE is a viral disease that can affect the brain and for which vaccination is recommended, while Lyme disease is a bacterial infection that can be treated with antibiotics. Full-covering clothing and skin inspection The most important protection against ticks is to wear full-covering clothing, especially for children who often play in grass and bushes. Thin trousers and pulled up socks reduce the risk of ticks attaching to the skin. Bright clothes also make it easier to spot the little crawlers. - We cover the children from the sun, but we also need to think about ticks. Inspect the skin regularly, especially where the skin is thin such as in the groin, knee folds and behind the ears, says Johan Holmgren. Ticks thrive where it's warm and humid, and can crawl around for a while before biting. Therefore, it is important to look extra carefully at the whole body after going out, not least at small children. How to remove a tick Although tick bites can feel worrying, the vast majority are harmless. But if you discover a tick, it is important to remove it as quickly as possible, just to be safe. Tweezers work great - grab the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull straight out. Special tools exist, but the most important thing is that you feel comfortable with what you use. - Removing a tick is not something we need to seek treatment for. We do that ourselves at home, says Johan Holmgren. Then wash the skin with soap and water. If you develop symptoms such as fever, headache or a rash that spreads, you should contact the health service, as this may indicate TBE or Lyme disease.

The breakthrough came only in 2023, when investigators reopened the case, held new interviews and were able to send the DNA found at the scene for analysis.  In 2025, the podcast "Who Killed Roxanne" was released, which went through the case. A tip number was also linked to the podcast, which led to new information and new witness information.  Four men arrested Last week, four men, all over 60, were arrested. Two of them were already in prison for other crimes, while one was arrested in Ohio and one at his home in Covington. All of them come from Covington and are said to have had connections with each other in 1982. They are suspected of aggravated rape and murder. The podcast was crucial A police officer who worked on the case said during a press conference that there was a "culture built on fear" in the city, which made the investigation difficult. He also highlighted the importance of the podcast for the investigation. - It played a decisive role in giving us the information we needed. "Cold cases don't solve themselves" Even though so many years have passed since Roxanne Sharp was murdered, the police have continued to work to find the culprits. "This case is a clear example of what persistence, cooperation and technological advances in investigative work can achieve," said prosecutor Collin Sims in a statement.  "For over four decades, the victim and her family have waited for answers. Today's arrests demonstrate our unwavering commitment to justice." Covington Police Chief Michael Ferrell said during a press conference that "cold cases don't solve themselves." - They are cleared because people show up, year after year, and refuse to give up. - He was cheerful and happy, but it could still have gone badly, continues Torkel Norling. Hunting dogs particularly affected According to the animal insurance company Agria, the number of dogs injured by wild boar increased by 30 percent last year. - It will always happen, but the risks are much smaller if we take our responsibility. Major environmental damage The drone attacks have turned Tuapse, usually a popular tourist destination for Russians, into a toxic inferno. The first wave led to an oil spill in the Black Sea and the attack on April 20, which took four days to extinguish and was visible from space, caused oil to rain over the city, writes Meduza. The Ukrainian military now considers energy facilities as legitimate military targets, as they provide the Russian war machine with fuel and money. A month ago, Russia banned all gasoline exports until the end of July to prevent the Russians themselves from running out of oil. Close to half of Russia's oil export capacity has been destroyed following Ukrainian drone attacks, damage to cables and the boarding of ships in the Russian shadow fleet.

She was diagnosed with OCD and helped in the form of cognitive behavioral therapy, CBT, and medication. It made a big difference. - Day and night. I was so skeptical about medicine, because you have a great need for control. But in the end I had no other choice. Today I can live a completely normal life. It is clear that I have obsessive thoughts, but it does not take over my everyday life. Wants to help others with OCD Linda "Lola" Beer is open about her obsessions on social media to help others. - When you are in a relapse, it feels like there is no way out. You really are: "I'm going to lose it, be alone for the rest of my life." It would have been very nice for me to see someone who has come to the other side, she says in Nyhetsmorgon. Many people with obsessive thoughts think they have gone crazy, says Christian Rück, senior physician and professor at Karolinska Institutet. Then it can be helpful to see others in the same situation. - Just to understand that there is something called OCD, there is a treatment and there are others who have this. It is a great relief for many.

The United States is falling The change is taking place mainly in authoritarian states, where laws that are actually meant to fight terrorism or espionage are used to silence journalists. But the trend also seeps into democracies.  The United States is a country whose freedom of the press is crumbling. It has fallen seven positions in the index and now lands in place 64. Erik Larsson points to President Donald Trump's rhetoric as an explanation.  Trump attacks the media daily. He wants to portray himself as an outsider. Larsson is concerned about various laws that limit journalists' opportunities to work, such as bans on photography at police stations and other protected objects. The white-backed woodpecker used to be quite common in Sweden. When deciduous forests disappeared during the 20th century, it lost its habitat.

The area has been temporarily closed to protect the birds.

- We have brought out deciduous trees and taken down spruce and conifers to get the trunks illuminated by the sun. Then the insects that are the staple food for the white-backed woodpecker thrive, says Åsa Stenman.

The goal is to reach around 20 breeding pairs by 2029. Last year there were 13–14.

- It is an acutely threatened species and we have so few in Sweden right now, she says. Can affect building plans At the same time, the protection of the species can affect development in Umeå. On the Island in the central city, the county board has said no to certain measures linked to housing construction. The decision has been appealed and will be tried in the Land and Environment Court.

- Since a few years ago, we have started to make an area slightly upstream of the river to make it more favorable for this species. Then it may be that white-backed woodpeckers will be seen on the island in the future as well, says Mikael Berglund (S), chairman of the building committee in Umeå. Benefits other species The White-backed Woodpecker is a so-called umbrella species, which means that the protection of its habitat also benefits many other species in the same forest.

- It has a foraging area that is significantly larger than the breeding area, but it is not the case that the island will become a large asphalt surface, rather there will still be quite a lot of forest and such areas there as well, says Mikael Berglund.

He describes fighting play as a combination of fighting, body contact and interaction. - These are games where you hunt, catch and putt quite lively and intense games. But Pilo Stylin emphasizes that risks are a natural part of children's development. - It must be allowed to go wrong sometimes, so that the children learn to manage their own and other people's emotions, he says. He also highlights the importance of differentiating between play fighting and so-called prank fights, which are more often connected to power plays and bullying. - Fundamental to all play is that it is based on free will and reciprocity. "We are working to create a picture of the extent of the leak and are actively working to minimize it," writes the company Instructure in a press release. The leak was discovered on Friday and is now said to be under control. 

According to the company, the hackers have, among other things, come across names and email addresses. "So far we cannot see that any passwords, social security numbers or financial information have been leaked". "Afraid that all information may be cleared" According to Tony Ottosson Gadd, IT manager at the University of Gothenburg, the security problems should be fixed - but at the moment it is not possible to confirm the extent of the incident or whether the hacker group's information is correct.
The University of Gothenburg plans to report the incident to the Swedish Data Protection Agency (IMY) and will also inform any victims. - It is clear that victims must be informed quickly, but right now we do not know what information may have actually been leaked. We fear that all information may be cleared, but we cannot assess the whole yet, says Tony Ottosson Gadd.

The platform is used by over 30 Swedish universities and colleges. Although the platform should not contain sensitive personal data, names and e-mail addresses in themselves may pose risks. - Such information can be used in other ways, for example resold or used for other attacks, says Tony Ottosson Gadd. Canvas also has functions where students can communicate with each other. As previously mentioned, the system is not built to handle sensitive information - but at the same time, it cannot be guaranteed that such information does not appear in the chats. Young western hacker group ShinyHunters, which took responsibility for the leak, writes that they have come across 3.65 terabytes of data containing information on 275 million students from 9,000 educational institutions.  - They are behind many other attacks. For Niklas Olsson in Örnsköldsvik, it started when he stopped playing football and ice hockey and would take care of his training in his spare time.

Accustomed to hard driving, he quickly got results in the gym and praise from those around him. He looked healthy and fit, but his body was slowly breaking down and exercise became a compulsion – as did healthy food.

When his body couldn't take it anymore, he sought medical attention and was advised about a treatment specifically for orthorexia. No diagnosis in Sweden Orthorexia is not a medical diagnosis in Sweden, which means that the sufferer must pay for their own treatment.

- It is a big and growing problem. When we started many years ago, there were 3-4 people per month who contacted us about these problems. Now there are 3-4 callers per day, says Yvonne Lin, Master of Medicine and CBT therapist.

Today's search for the perfect body often takes place in the public eye. Exercise influencers attract tens of thousands of followers and the boundaries of both exercise and healthy food are being pushed.

- In the beginning, there were many fitness people who sought care. Now there are also elite athletes and regular exercisers. Everyone wants to get stronger and starts banning food for themselves, says Yvonne Lin.

- Step by step you remove sugar, white flour, cakes, desserts, red meat and at the same time continue to train hard. It affects the body's major physiological systems, she adds. 101572ce69033abdb556af42b335c36d82818dce: New figures: Staying in the country - and continuing to commit crimes
20add578d62af149d3e5b6b15cc03013c318d43d:
Brå has produced statistics for roughly 6,000 people with deportation orders who served a prison sentence in Sweden between the years 2013 and 2023. 

During the investigated period, an average of 48 percent of these people had their deportation enforced, i.e. left the country. The proportion has increased - but at the end of the measurement period it was still lower than 60 percent.

- It is important to point out that we will never achieve 100 percent. There are legal guidelines for which countries Sweden may deport to, if there is a war going on or if the person is at risk of torture. There can be practical problems such as the lack of a return agreement in the country you want to deport to, says Johanna Viberg, investigator at Brå. Recidivism Many therefore remain in Sweden as a result of obstacles to enforcement - sometimes for many years. Brå's statistics show that one in five commits new crimes during that time. The most common are theft and burglary, drug offenses are also common.

Brå themselves believe that there are many misconceptions regarding deported people who relapse into crime - and that many do not seem to know that less than half are actually deported in the end.

- There are many people who do not know that it is a relatively large percentage of deportation decisions that are not actually enforced. You hear in the political debate that there are more people to be sentenced to deportation, but it is important that you see the real effect of these decisions that are made. It risks being more symbolic than having the intended effect otherwise, Johanna Viberg continues. Minister: "Has responsibility" Migration Minister Johan Forsell is not satisfied with today's situation - but puts his faith in harsher punishments - and several deportation decisions:

 - I have a responsibility, and that is exactly why we are tightening the legislation, says Migration Minister Johan Forsell (M). - Now Sweden actually gets the toughest legislation for criminal deportations in the entire Nordic region. All persons convicted of an offense with a more severe penalty than a fine must be deported

On May 9 every year, Russia celebrates the victory over Nazi Germany in World War II. But this year, the victory parade is canceled in 15 regions, the Russian opposition website ASTRA reports, citing a statement from Russian authorities.

- They can't afford military equipment, and they fear that drones can buzz over Red Square, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the other day

In Moscow, among other places, large military demonstrations of power at Red Square do not take place. It is the first time since 2007 that this has happened. Fears Ukrainian attacks Russia expert Malcolm Dixelius sees this as a sign that Moscow fears Ukrainian attacks. - It is primarily a sign that the Ukrainian drone attacks are successful, says Russia expert Malcolm Dixelius. In several parts of the country, the celebration is held in a greatly reduced form. "A sign of weakness" In St. Petersburg, the victory parade will be held without armored vehicles. In other cities, the celebration is conducted online. - That Putin slims down the parade in Moscow is a sign of weakness. Then local authorities do not dare to order the population out, with the risk of them becoming the target of the next swarm of Ukrainian drones, says Dixelius. Russian authorities severely restricted Victory Day celebrations starting in 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began, but not to this extent. The Russian Defense Ministry has warned Ukraine against trying to disrupt the parade. As in previous years during the war, Russia has simultaneously declared a ceasefire.

5320c06d2c5cbf76c0e3dae9cbf017d1c782a323: The theory that the hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius may have originated from a bird-watching trip at a landfill in Argentina is now being questioned by infection control experts.  The outbreak is believed to have occurred while the ship was on an expedition in southern South America and Antarctica, with around 150 passengers and around 70 crew members on board. At least three people have died after contracting the disease, including an elderly couple from the Netherlands who are said to have been among the first infected. According to Björn Olsen, professor of infectious diseases at Uppsala University, it is unlikely that bird watching would have been the source of infection. - It is unreasonable. I think so, he says. The background is information to the news agency AP from two Argentinian officials who anonymously stated that a Dutch couple may have been exposed to hantavirus, in this case the serious spirit virus, while bird watching at a garbage dump in southern Argentina - and then brought the infection on board the cruise ship. Garbage dumps and treatment plants Björn Olsen, who is a bird watcher himself, emphasizes that hantavirus does indeed occur in rodents in the Andes, but that the risk of infection when bird watching in itself is low. - We bird watchers often look at birds at landfills, sewage treatment plants and mud puddles. But there you are not particularly exposed to rodents, he says. Instead, Olsen points to another and much more likely route of infection. - You have slept over in a simpler place where there are rodents. The rodents have had this virus in them, peed it out and then it has spread to humans. That is by far the most likely explanation, he says. According to Olsen, the risk is greatest when staying overnight in environments where rodents are present - not when staying outdoors. - That's what I thought from the beginning, when I heard about this outbreak, he says. Similar to severe pneumonia Hantavirus is spread when people inhale dust containing the virus from dried urine or faeces from infection

The rainforest creates its own rain One reason is that the Amazon acts as a giant water pump. The trees absorb water from the ground and release it as water vapor. That moisture then falls back as rain over the rainforest. According to the researchers, the Amazon generates up to half of its own precipitation. - The rainforest thus creates large parts of its own rain, says Johan Rockström. When large areas are cut down, the forest becomes drier and gradually loses the ability to keep this moisture circulation going. Then the drought risks spreading over huge areas. The study also shows that deforestation in one location can affect rainfall hundreds or thousands of kilometers away. If the rainforest is broken down, large amounts of the carbon risk being released into the atmosphere and fueling global warming even further. f7f44e2f9c3c6ce86a0f189858d71256fe49eca5: The tourist favorite tightens the rules - thousands of accommodations disappear
4cd8fd6036525a3ffcdfb17ffc44de80b6aa9f88: In the popular seaside town of Biarritz, short-term rentals via Airbnb have long been a profitable business. But in recent years, the regulations have been tightened considerably. When a transition period expired in March this year, it meant that around 10,000 homes may no longer be rented out in the same way as before. - In principle, I have lost almost all my customers in the last year, says Swedish Sophia Paulin, who worked to help home owners rent out their homes in Biarritz. Growing housing crisis The background to the new rules is a growing housing crisis. For several years, more and more homes have been bought up to be rented out to tourists, which has pushed up prices and made it difficult for locals to find accommodation. - It's frustrating not being able to stay where you grew up and work, says Matisse Dailly, who works in a shop in central Biarritz. He describes how many homes were empty for large parts of the year - or were rented out on short contracts that forced tenants to move out during the summer months, when the apartments could instead be rented out at significantly higher prices via Airbnb. The new rules mean that in practice it has become significantly more difficult to rent out homes that are not even permanent residences. In order to rent out, it is now required either that you live in the home yourself most of the year - or that you compensate by creating a new home for long-term rental. Anyone who tries to circumvent the rules risks heavy fines. A local resident tells how she received a letter from the municipality threatening up to 1,000 euros a day if she continues to rent out. Changed neighborhood At the same time, several testify that the neighborhood has changed. - It has become more that you keep an eye on each other, says Sophia Paulin. What the effect will be in the longer term remains to be seen. The summer of 2026 will be the first real test of what the rules actually mean. - The people of Biarritz want Biarritz back - that's what this is all about, says Sophia Paulin.

When it comes to ants, Thomas Persson Vinnersten, biologist and pest expert, believes that the most important thing is to keep them outside. - Maybe you know where they get in? It might be under the gap in the patio door or through a crack. Close there, he says in Nyhetsmorgon. Housewife trick: cinnamon It's also important to keep clean. - Spring has not really started everywhere. Then they look inside and find what we leave behind: crumbs, ice cream or juice - they love it. Wipe clean, use a dishcloth, says Thomas Persson Vinnersten. An effective housewife's tip is to disrupt their sense of smell with, for example, cinnamon or cayenne pepper at the point where they enter the house, if you cannot seal.  Right now, the wasp queens are starting to probe the terrain for where to build this year's nest. ffb0ec457bc697fd3d9eab915144c0d40fb438a3:
In Skåne, a new method is being tested to protect spring rape fields from rape beetles. At Gunnarhögs Gård in Österlen, some of the rapeseed blooms earlier to attract the pests.

- We hope that they will attack the victim plants so that the large amount, 93 percent, will be protected from these rape beetles, says farmer Anja Persson at Gunnarshög's farm. 

So-called sacrificial plants grow on seven percent of the field. The idea is that the canola beetles should gather there, instead of in the main crop. Feeds on the canola buds The canola beetle, which in English is called the pollen beetle, eats pollen but can also feed on the small tender buds of the rapeseed early in the season. Then the canola can stop flowering - but in the experiment, the idea is that the rams fly to the victim plants instead.

Agronomist and rapeseed expert Albin Gunnarsson is following the trial on the farm and believes that so far it looks promising.

- I feel that this year this has worked quite well. The canola beetles have been in these plants and they certainly do damage there, but they do damage in a place in the field where it is of marginal importance, he says.

Rapeseed is globally the third most important oil crop after soybean and oil palm. In Sweden, it is grown above all in Skåne, where the yellow fields are a typical sign of early summer. Whether the rape beetles continue to "go for the trick" remains to be seen. "Still an attempt" For farmer Anja Persson, the method is new - and the uncertainty remains. - It's the very first time and it's a bit new for us and we hope it will turn out well. But it's still an attempt. We don't really know how it will turn out. We also have a trap that indicates whether it is time or not, she says.

In the long term, she hopes that the method will reduce the need for control.
- We hope that it will lead to less control, that you don't need to have as much plant protection products as you had before, says Anja Persson.

Now the government is putting forward a crisis package of SEK 17.5 billion to support households and businesses. - Swedish families and businesses must have access to energy around the clock, all year round - at reasonable and reasonable prices, says Energy and Industry Minister Ebba Busch (KD) during a press conference. The mothers then continued to take capsules of either kale or carrot powder several times a week until delivery.  The children were then followed up at about three weeks of age and again at three years of age, when twelve of them remained in the study. Their facial reactions were examined in the fetal stage with ultrasound and after birth with video recordings.  Reacted differently The researchers found that the babies exposed to the carrot before birth showed less negative reactions when they later smelled a carrot top, but grimaced at the smell of kale. Corresponding reactions were seen in the children exposed to kale.  What we see over time is that children still respond more favorably to vegetables that they were exposed to in the womb. This may indicate that exposure to a certain taste at the end of pregnancy can create a long-term taste or smell memory that can potentially influence their food preferences in the years after birth, Nadja Reissland, professor at the University of Durham and lead author of the study, told The Guardian.  More studies are needed The researchers emphasize, however, that the investigated group is small and that more and larger studies are needed to investigate whether the effect is significant for the children's actual consumption of vegetables.  They also highlight that the children may have been exposed to the flavors via breast milk in the weeks after birth, and that genetic differences in smell and taste perception may have influenced the results.

The bottle washed ashore in Poland, where it was found by a winter bather who saved it without opening it. After his passing, the son inherited the bottle and left it unopened for another 16 years. A film was decisive. It was only after the son saw the film "Message in a Bottle" with Kevin Costner that he decided to look for the mail in a bottle again. - Then the son thought it was time to open the bottle, says Carin Hellqvist with a smile. With the help of a friend in Sundsvall, he then managed to track down the Hellqvist couple. - We thought about the bottle mail a few weeks after the trip, but then it fell into oblivion. And then they haven't thought about it for 20 years. You don't think about a bottle, says Carin Hellqvist. Unexpected contact Getting in touch after such a long time was a surprise for the couple, who had never guessed that their bottle mail would receive a response. - It feels very strange. It's almost 21 years since we threw this bottle overboard, says Carin Hellqvist.

Attracted with money and affiliation The recruitment of girls and boys looks different, according to Stephan Kiernan. Many girls are not directly involved in the gangs, but take assignments in what is called "crime as a service", where criminal schemes are presented in chats. Other girls enter the environments through a love affair with an older criminal, according to Stephan Kiernan.  The girls who are recruited Anna Danielsson from the social administration in Gothenburg warns of a number of risk factors that parents should be aware of.  - But the profiling has also changed in step with social media, where basically anyone can be recruited from the safe sphere that is the home.  Risk factors include girls who have difficulties in school with high absenteeism. But also socializing with older friends who are connected to organized crime. Another pilot says that the Swedish forces have potential - but that they need to improve their drones and their tactics. ÖB: Must listen to Ukraine Now Sweden's Commander-in-Chief Michael Claesson says that all NATO allies must listen to Ukraine's experiences and "as quickly as possible" learn how to carry out military operations with drones. That position is shared by the Americans on the ground. So far in May (up to and including the 14th), the electricity price is close to one kroner per kilowatt hour (kWh) in southernmost Sweden, slightly lower in electricity area 3 (Svealand and northern Götaland). More unusual is that the price is also high in Norrland, almost 70 öre, according to the prices on the electricity exchange Nord Pool. The reason is the weak hydrology (water availability in nature) that we have been struggling with since the low-precipitation winter, says Sigvardsson. Connection to Europe This leads to less and more expensive electricity from hydropower. When several nuclear power reactors are currently shut down for annual maintenance, the price effect becomes extra clear. With the weak hydrology, hydropower is forced to limit its production despite the high electricity prices. Sweden as a whole is then forced to limit exports to the south and then gets a stronger price link with the rest of Europe, where electricity prices are higher, says Christian Holtz, electricity analyst at the consulting agency Merlin & Metis. The high price of gas on the continent, which is used for electricity production in Germany, among others, is connected to the war in the Middle East and the closed Strait of Hormuz. Higher prices On the other hand, more and more solar power is causing electricity prices to drop to minus in the middle of the day, and then skyrocket in the evening. The price differences are extreme. And for those who can control their consumption, there is money to be had. Johan Sigvardsson throws out another warning flag for even higher electricity prices in the future. So we possibly have a super El Niño going on this summer and autumn, which in that case brings heat (which increases the need for electricity-sucking air conditioning) and drought. There are clearly risks to even higher prices what it suffers. Now the electricity price itself makes up far from the entire electricity bill. On top of the exchange-traded electricity price, electricity tax, VAT and electricity grid fee of well over one kroner per kWh are added.

Recycled chorus arouses criticism At the same time, some have reacted that the chorus in "Live forever" is reminiscent of music that Thomas Stenström previously used in the TV series "Live life". - If you want to make a memorable and special World Cup song, I think it's best not to reuse old material, says Tina Mehrafzoon. At the same time, she emphasizes that it is common for artists to build on previous ideas. - Thomas Stenström is free to make his creative choices. According to Mehrafzoon, the song's future status will largely be determined by how the Swedish men's national team fares in the championship. - Make Sweden an incredible World Cup, this song will have a much greater cultural significance for us Swedes.

6a58cc0b02a002da26ed6ac4d9ca30cf0cc79363:
Mikaela Åhlin-Kottulinsky is facing one of the biggest challenges of her career when, together with three other drivers, she must drive as many laps as possible in one day at the Nürburgring in Germany. The classic 24-hour race has been organized since 1970 and this year attracts around 300,000 spectators. 
Formula 1 star Max Verstappen is also on the starting line. - It is the most brutal race that exists in track racing, says Åhlin-Kottulinsky. 300,000 fans are expected at the track Nürburgring is known for its fast turns and extreme weather changes. The drivers can face both sunshine, torrential rain and hail during the same lap. - You can start the lap dry on slicks and suddenly there is hail in the middle of the track, she says. In addition to the weather, driving through the night on a track without street lighting also awaits. Motorsport runs in the family. Mikaela's grandfather Freddy Kottulinsky won two races at the Nürburgring in the 1970s, and her mother has also competed in rallying. - Grandfather's name is already here among the winners. It would be great to be able to add another Kottulinsky name, she says. The fatal accident shakes the sport The classic track is also known for its risks. In April, Finnish racing driver Juha Miettinen died in an accident at the Nürburgring. - When something like that happens, it comes close. We all know that motorsport entails risks, says Åhlin-Kottulinsky. At the same time, she emphasizes that safety must always come first. - The best thing we can do is to continue competing with safety as the highest priority. Before the debut, she recharges with sleep, food and focus and looks forward to the audience party. - You have to be here to understand the feeling. Everything just breathes motorsport in every fiber.

5e5b99fdf22e2532eb3ff443baa4313ea07e48c6: Xi Jinping is known to have a total lack of charisma. The contrast between the austere Chinese leader and the wildly swinging American president could not be greater.  Trump seeks quick lucrative deals and short-term victories. Xi, on the other hand, is playing a strategic game in the longer term. The fact that he is no longer playing for the United States became evident during Trump's state visit. It was the American president who farted. Trump praised Xi for being "a brilliant leader" and "a wonderful guy." And did not pretend that Xi Jinping actually threatened the US with a military conflict if it does not do as the Chinese want and drop its support for self-governing Taiwan.  Cool media interest A sign of China's new self-confidence is that an American state visit did not even end up on the front page of the state-controlled Chinese media. On the day Trump arrived, the English-language China Daily topped instead with a picture of Xi Jinping shaking hands with the president of Tajikistan. For a long time, the position of the United States as the only real global superpower has been a matter of course. The US is still militarily completely superior. But the failed attack on Iran shows that there are limits to what can be achieved with bombs alone. Trump's erratic and aggressive foreign policy makes many people see China as a more stable alternative in world politics. When Donald Trump launched his tariff war, many leaders rushed to China to strengthen trade relations. Chlamydia is already the most common sexually transmitted disease in Europe, with 213,443 cases in 2024. It also tops the list in Sweden, but the situation is quite stable, says Crawford. The United Arab Emirates has repeatedly been the target of Iranian attacks across the Gulf. The country has expressed anger that other Gulf states did not want to implement a collective retaliation against Iran. Dissatisfaction culminated in April in an unexpected decision to leave the Opec oil cartel. Now cooperation appears to have improved, and the UAE is increasingly leaning towards a settlement, rather than violence, as a better way forward. What the United States should focus on most right now is getting Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz, the country believes, and is supported by Saudi Arabia, according to Bloomberg's sources. Qatar takes mediator role Until now, Pakistan has had the main responsibility as a mediator in the war. Now Qatar is also stepping into the role of mediator. On Friday, a Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran to present a new peace proposal, sources told Reuters. Qatar's trip is said to have been coordinated with the US and aims to "reach a final agreement that will end the war and resolve the issues with Iran".

The US has a hand in the game US President Donald Trump has repeatedly said he wants to make Canada the 51st US state. According to Christophe Premat, director of the Center for Canadian Studies at Stockholm University, the play may have contributed to what is happening in Alberta right now.

 - I think it has caused the separatist movement, says Christophe Premat.  In Alberta, the provincial government is led by Premier Danielle Smith, who belongs to the Conservative Party. Alberta is known for its large oil and gas industry and also has many other natural resources. The province accounts for 84 percent of Canada's crude oil production.  - That is why the US was a little more interested in promoting that particular movement, says Christophe Premat.  Demand for independence nothing new But there is also a very different game behind it, according to Christophe Premat, who believes that for a long time there has been a culture in Western Canada where people want to have greater influence and often oppose the decisions of the government in Ottawa. - It is more of a ploy against the federal government, says Christophe Premat. 

Independence requirements are nothing new in Canada. The province of Québec has previously held two referendums on secession from the rest of the country. According to Christophe Premat, Canada is fundamentally more divided than many people think.  - There will be a fight between both provinces when they have to try to defend certain issues, such as environmental issues vis-a-vis the oil industry or the fossil industry and such things that are discussed at the parliament in Ottawa, says Christophe Premat. Sandra Lindstedt is a thoracic surgeon and lecturer at Lund University and hopes that the method will be able to be used in healthcare in the future. - If we can develop the method, the hope is that we will be able to use it as a screening tool, much like mammography, she explains. But Prime Minister Andrej Babiš won the election last year with campaign promises to increase pensions and improve healthcare. Now he is going against Donald Trump's demand that Europe increase its defense spending. Just like Pedro Sánchez in Spain. But Sánchez is a socialist and Babiš is a right-wing populist. "Our military is a joke" Geography may play a role. The Czech Republic is surrounded by other NATO countries and non-aligned Austria. The threat from Russia is not as close as for Poland, which shares a border with the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad. There is also a vocal minority in the Czech Republic that prefers Putin's Russia as a partner to the EU. But despite that, polls show that a majority of Czechs actually want a stronger defense. - We have to invest more money. So, our military is a joke, says Prague resident Andrej Novotný to TV4. Sweden invests Alžběta Černá, who also lives in Prague, says, however, that the government should invest more in social programs instead. - Here in the Czech Republic there are other areas that need the money more, she says. After a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Babiš changed the tone a bit. The Czech Republic may be able to reach two percent soon, he said. 2f0ca20c310303f8688284c3a8f8f9dc97b5fd72: Several banks lower mortgage interest rates - the expert: "Negotiate mode"
e64ca32d7901af58abffbf347701a526f101cd3a: When war broke out in the Middle East, the banks raised interest rates quickly, as the market feared rising inflation and more rate hikes from the Riksbank. But now the situation has calmed down somewhat and the banks' costs for financing mortgages have decreased again. This has led to SBAB, Danske Bank, SEB and Sandia lowering their variable mortgage rates during the week. Good time to negotiate Frida Bratt, financial journalist at Dagens Industri och Privata Affärer, believes that it is a good time to discuss your terms with the bank. She emphasizes the importance of being aware that banks' financing costs have gone down and that this is a strong argument in negotiations. - Negotiate with the bank. It is a good time to do it right now, says Frida Bratt. At the same time, the outside world is still shaky and there is great uncertainty in the financial market. Bratt points out that the banks are generally quicker to raise than to lower interest rates, and that the reductions so far have been smaller than the previous increases. She therefore recommends mortgage borrowers to be prepared for different scenarios, depending on how the situation in the world develops. Be prepared to change banks One of Frida Bratt's most important pieces of advice is to compare conditions between different banks and be prepared to change if you get better offers. - If you threaten to change banks if you don't get good terms, you must be prepared to take action. It's not that hard to change banks, she says. She also believes that it may be wise to use both facts, such as the fact that several banks have already lowered, and the possibility of changing banks as arguments in the negotiation. More banks are expected to follow Bratt believes that more banks will probably follow the four that have already lowered interest rates. She believes that the banks often look at each other and that credibility is at stake. - They raised when funding costs rose - then they also have to lower when funding costs fall. Otherwise, they might as well be honest that they want to earn more on the mortgage, says Frida Bratt

aa286390de40edb663a7e7db351c6e02b576c43e: Almost half of Sweden's homeowners have at some point been in conflict with a neighbor. Nevertheless, the quarrels are rarely about big issues, but about things that rub off on everyday life. This is shown by a new report from the Swedish Association of Villa Owners. - The report shows that neighbor issues both touch and upset, says Lisa Hjelm, communications manager. The conflicts often arise over recurring small things such as sounds, animals or how Santa is looked after. Barking dogs, loud parties and cats roaming freely in plots are at the top of the list of things that disturb the most. Small behaviors disturb more than noise One example that stands out, however, is not about noise or smoke, but about everyday behavior. - I would say that neighbors who don't say hello, that bothers you. It feels like the easiest thing to do something about. It actually comes before problems with grillos and things like that. Then it's more disturbing that people don't greet each other, says Hjelm. One explanation for the conflicts is how neighborhoods work in Sweden. - Sweden stands out when it comes to neighborhood legislation. Here there are not so many rules to adhere to, but rather codes of conduct that may be tacitly agreed upon. That you should show consideration, be nice and contribute to the common good, she says. This means that many Swedes can avoid the worst mosquito plagues this summer. "Mosquito-free is a bit of a stretch, but fewer and smaller pools produce fewer mosquitoes," notes Anders Lindström. The species that hatch in permanent watercourses are not affected as much by the drought and, as usual, arrive later in the summer - but they are fewer in number than those that hatch in the spring surge. According to US court documents, 303 gold bars, worth $40 million (372 million kroner), were found in the man's house in West Virginia. Lied about his background The man has worked at a post in the American intelligence service where he had access to top secret documents. According to former employees, the suspect is said to have requisitioned large amounts of gold and cash for work-related expenses from the US government, which he also received. According to the FBI, however, only a fraction of the money and gold was in the storage space that was to be used.  The investigation also shows that the suspect lied about his background, and among other things claimed that he was a pilot in the US Navy. He has also claimed that he has dual degrees from the schools Clemson University and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, which also does not seem to be true. The man is now in custody and will be heard by a federal court in Virginia on Friday. Both the FBI and the CIA have declined to comment on the case, according to US media.

508e2a6a6866a72ff764cdf73e9915f004e4869f: Råd & rön has tested 13 popular hazelnut creams. In the test, a taste panel had to assess appearance, aroma, taste and texture, which were weighed together to form a taste rating. All products were also sent to labs to analyze unwanted substances. How "nutty" the hazelnut cream is varies. In the test, the hazelnut content is eight to 20 percent. This means that many products are rather a mixture where sugar, cocoa and various oils make up a large part of the content. "Too sweet" At the bottom of the test are Renée Voltaire and the classic Printzell's Nöt-Créme, known from the small bags of nut cream that have been around since the 1960s. Despite the nostalgia, Printzells gets the lowest rating from the taste panel. - You think it's too sweet and you miss the hazelnut taste, says Anna Edberg, test manager Råd & rön. Renée Voltaire gets mixed reviews in the tasting panel, but ends up last overall mainly because of the lab analysis. Traces of an unauthorized plasticizer were found there. The substance must not be present in this type of product, as it must not come into contact with fatty foods. Most expensive is worst Despite the fact that the levels that were discovered were low and not considered to pose any major health risk, it is still a deviation that should not be there. Renée Voltaire's hazelnut cream is also the most expensive in the test. Råd & rön and TV4 have contacted the company about the find. Renée Voltaire has replied that they take the results very seriously and that they have started their own quality analysis. They have also requested a review of processes, routines and raw materials.  Rigoni di Asiago Nocciolata Original also ends up at the bottom. It received mixed reviews in the taste panel and contained low levels of the plasticizer ATBC. See which hazelnut cream was the best in the test in the clip above.

It must have been given in liquid form and is available on the ward. In small doses it produces harmless tremors. In large doses, it disturbs the body's potassium, and then the heart beats incorrectly. - I have long hair at work, the colleagues around me describe that "the only thing we saw was a mere tuft going back and forth", because the whole body was shaking, says "Anna". Perhaps we will never know the whole truth The investigation into attempted murder was closed in April 2026 and the suspicions against the previously suspected female colleague were written off. "Anna" and "Linda" may never get the full answer to who was behind the poisoning and why.

- It is probably someone who has done this on purpose. So it was a very scary thought, says "Linda".

- It makes me sad and disappointed and afraid that someone else could be exposed to this again, says "Anna".

Instead, active substances, i.e. the actual active substances in medicines, are ordered from abroad and used to manufacture them illegally in Sweden. - Have you ever ordered from Amazon? It's really the same thing, says Martin Burman, investigator at the Medical Products Agency, about how substances are bought in from abroad. Ordered via open platforms According to the Medical Products Agency, trade takes place via large B2B platforms in China and India, among others. To avoid detection, passwords and loopholes are used. Substances can, for example, be hidden by re-spelling in advertisements. After initial contact, the dialogue moves on to encrypted channels such as WhatsApp, where payment can be made in cryptocurrencies such as bitcoin. The goods are then smuggled into Europe. - It is a legal platform on the surface, but it is used by criminal actors, says Burman. Moved production here At the same time, authorities are seeing a shift in how crimes are committed. In the past, it was mainly about finished medicines being smuggled into Sweden. Now instead, the manufacturing takes place in the country and in the rest of the EU, above all when it comes to slimming preparations. - There are many places where we also see illegal manufacturing taking place within Sweden and throughout the EU, says Burman. Police cases and judgments linked to pharmaceutical crimes have increased, and the authority sees a clear rise in both reports and seizures. Can be life-threatening The illegally manufactured medicines can pose great risks. At least 45 deaths in Sweden during 2024 and 2025 are linked to falsified medicines, something that the Pharmaceutical World has previously reported on. Manufacturing takes place without control and often without sterile environments, which is particularly problematic when it comes to injectable drugs. - You simply inject pollutants into the body. It can cause serious allergic reactions, says Burman. - It can get really bad if it spreads

In a customs document from a long time ago, you can read that snus was brought across the Swedish border from Finland in 1637. And what happened after that is, as they say, history.  But traveling with snus outside of Sweden is not easy these days. In the EU there are common regulations, but recently a number of countries have stepped away from them or expanded their rules. SEK 15,000 in fines The biggest restrictions on snuff are found in Singapore and since April 1 in France.  Singapore has zero tolerance for snuff, both brown and white. It may not be sold, imported, bought or used. Wearing snuff during a body check can mean a fine of up to SEK 15,000.  For entry into the country, the fines can be even higher and, in the worst case, even lead to imprisonment for up to six months. There, snus is seen as a drug. In France, white snus is the hardest hit. Since April 1 this year, it is forbidden to consume, import and transport.  White snus is classified under the same regulations as, for example, narcotics, which means that the punishment can be anything from up to 375,000 euros in fines or five years in prison.

The white snus can be bought in many European countries including Malta and Iceland. In Iceland, on the other hand, since 1997 there has been a ban on bringing in and selling brown snus into the country.  Want to see prescription Australia is known for its tough customs controls and strict regulations. As for brown snus, there is a maximum limit of 25 grams. If you take more with you, it must be declared and paid to customs. White snus is classified as a prescription drug and requires a medical certificate for import.

If you really want to be on the safe side, you also check what the rules for snuffing on board the flight look like.

284bdb27c1b5ba6e8d6c7014349f3fb2613721e7: The proposal: 15-year limit for social media
9093c1f5a2d99b294cf44cbbdc2147aa37ce90f9: Last autumn, the government appointed an investigation, led by Lisa Englund Krafft, which was tasked with reviewing the possibilities of introducing an age limit on social media. The first partial report has now been handed over to Social Affairs Minister Jacob Forssmed. And in it, an age limit of 15 years is proposed. Big challenge Children and young people under the age of 15 should not have access to logged-in mode on online platforms that enable users to discover, connect to, and communicate with each other, or where content can be shared or discovered. That's what Englund Krafft writes in the investigation. Screens and social media and their impact on the health of children and young people are one of the biggest challenges of our time, says Forssmed at a press conference. Research shows that social media affects young people's mental health in a negative way. Many children and young people are exposed to terrible things on their mobile phones, says Forssmed and adds: Protecting the health and safety of children and young people has been a priority task for me and the government. Age limits on social media have been introduced in several places in the world, and a total of work is underway on the issue in 35 countries, according to Unicef. Australia was the first to ban, when last December it introduced a 16-year age limit on ten different social media platforms, including Instagram, Tiktok and Snapchat. Since then, several countries have followed suit. The Philippines, Denmark and the UK are some of the countries that have plans to introduce stricter age limits on social media. Great support In Sweden, political support for an age limit is great. Social Democrats party leader Magdalena Andersson said last October that she wants to see a 15-year limit. We have previously regulated other addictive products. We need to do that here too, she said. In Sweden, there is currently a limit of 13 years for when children must have parental consent to create accounts on social media.

Armenia has long been heavily dependent on Russia, both security-wise and economically. Russia has already lost influence, not only in Ukraine and in the former Soviet Union, it has also lost Syria, Venezuela and other partners, says Jakob Hedenskog, analyst at the Center for Eastern European Studies at the Foreign Policy Institute. The Kremlin monitors the election The Kremlin has been accused of trying to influence the election through disinformation. Vladimir Putin is likely to be watching the elections in Armenia closely, for fear of losing yet another ally if Pashinyan remains in power.

Many Armenians are disappointed with old ally Russia, which did not come to the country's aid when neighboring Azerbaijan seized the Nagorno-Karabakh region three years ago. For two years, Armenia and Azerbaijan have been negotiating a peace agreement, without a final result. - Pashinyan is a politician who pursues a policy to resolve the conflict with Azerbaijan and he sees that a relationship with the EU makes it possible to make Armenia less dependent on Russia. Young people more skeptical But despite outstretched hands to the West, it is not obvious that Pasjinjan is a pro-EU politician, says Jakob Hedenskog. - He is primarily a power politician. He is quite a polarizing politician, with a rather fractious message and he is not afraid to antagonize other Armenian political groups.

Among the Armenian population, there is also a significant number who do not trust Pashinjan at all. Many of the skeptics are young people, says Jakob Hedenskog. - Pasjinian's support is above all in rural areas among the older part of the population, while the young people are considerably more skeptical of him.

258cc45d755258d556944bca374751ac8f0c5725: This is how AI will help researchers find dangerous ticks
c808886a4bcc7d8d033a786b5cf7dffe65b13414: 35,000 tick images have been submitted by the users of the tick app "Report a tick" to the Norwegian Veterinary Institute, SVA, since the app was launched three years ago.  But reviewing each image takes time, and so the researchers now want to use AI for help. - There will always still be a need for a human behind, but AI could quickly look through the images and see if there is something special that we are particularly interested in; for example, ticks that are not found in Sweden today and that can carry new viruses or bacteria, says Anna Omazic, tick researcher at SVA. Knew nothing about ticks It is species such as the dreaded migratory bird tick, Hyalomma marginatum, that the researchers hope will be alerted by the AI ​​model if they are discovered. The migratory bird tick can carry hemorrhagic fever and can chase its prey for up to 200 meters. So far, only a few specimens have appeared in Sweden and luckily they don't seem to survive very well in our climate. Najmeh Abiri, who is a lecturer in machine learning at Malmö University, knew nothing about ticks before Anna Omazic at SVA contacted the university to get help developing the AI ​​model for the tick app - but now she has a great interest in the small animals. Getting the AI ​​model to be able to directly determine the species of the ticks based on the public's photos, however, has not proven to be so simple. - The quality of the photos varies a lot, lighting and so on - and it's also not easy to take a picture of a tick that is in motion, explains Najmeh Abiri. "That would be the dream" The researchers hope to be able to launch the AI ​​model within one or two years - and the goal is to also involve our neighboring countries in order to quickly receive signals about new findings of dangerous ticks. - That we in northern Europe could have a common app, which you could enter information into, and that researchers could access all the data at the same time, that would be the dream, says Najmeh Abiri.

- We have asked our staff, both research staff and nursing staff, how do you use the medical library today and how would you like it in the future? The uniform answers we get are that the library is in the computer. It is the digital that is in demand, says Göran Larsson, Director of Research and Education at the Västerbotten region.

The number of study places will remain, but for the students the books have been an important part of the study environment.

- To sit here and study when it is completely empty, there is no interior design, there is a lonely bookshelf, then you are not so motivated to study, but then you just become depressed, says Emelie Strandh.

The probability of two increases is around 50 percent in pricing right now. A palpable bang If the market is right, it will be a palpable bang for many households. If the interest rate on a mortgage of three million were raised by 0.50 percentage points, it would increase the cost of the loan by SEK 15,000 per year - if you ignore the effects of the interest deduction. In addition to the ECB's potential series of hikes this year, global interest rates are being pushed upwards since the interest rate market in the US has started to change legs. The likelihood of interest rate cuts in the world's largest economy this year has basically been erased after a fresh load of unexpectedly strong jobs figures on Friday. Increased risk of higher interest rates comes at the same time as the prices of fuel and electricity are pushed up by the energy price shock from the closed Strait of Hormuz in the wake of the now more than 100-day-long Iran war.

Yesterday, the figure was presented showing that inflation in the US is the highest in three years. Inflation for May is 4.2 percent. The reason is above all increased fuel and energy prices. But price increases on other goods as well are slowly beginning to be felt by the Americans.

There is no other single issue that matters more to voters when they elect a new Congress in November. Trump knows this, of course. Finance and wallet issues are always important in US elections. And so it is best to cover up the truth.  When the president was asked to comment on the inflation figure, he therefore said:

- I love the inflation. Reagan: "Inflation is as violent as a robber" Trump is probably the only high-ranking leader who has ever praised inflation. Loving inflation is, to say the least, a different way of expressing yourself about something that strongly affects Americans' everyday lives. Since inflation means price increases, it is political suicide to celebrate it.  Trump's Republican successor, President Ronald Reagan, described it diametrically differently in the late seventies, when the United States was plagued by very high inflation:

"Inflation is as violent as a robber, as terrifying as an armed thief and as deadly as an assassin".

Most Americans who live with increased prices in their everyday lives probably find it easier to agree with Reagan's description than with Trump's. The choice is made at the petrol pump and in the supermarket.

Midsummer weather split in two Next week, ahead of midsummer, the high pressure will strengthen over Sweden, causing the cooler air to shift further east. It brings slightly higher temperatures - but the rain is on its way. - The country looks like it will be divided in two. The northern half a little more low pressure with rain showers now and then with 15-18 degrees. While in the southern half it becomes more stable with, as it looks right now, a high pressure ridge growing in with sunny weather and temperatures between 20-25 degrees. It will be sunniest on the coasts. But the forecast is still relatively uncertain and can change, says Madeleine Westin.  Rainier July than normal If you look further ahead, the forecasts become more uncertain. The European weather centers have compiled several weather forecasts and according to them, July will be a little rainier than normal in Central Sweden. In the northern parts, warmer temperatures than normal are expected. - You have 50-70 percent accuracy from these weather forecasts, says Madeleine Westin.  High temperatures and drought in August Over Western Europe, the high pressure looks set to stop, bringing high temperatures and possible drought. The drought stretches right into August. Large parts of Sweden get fairly normal temperatures. - If we look at the precipitation deviation, it looks like northern Sweden is getting a little more rain than usual in the month of August, while it is getting drier in both Götaland and Svealand, says Westin.

In 2025, roughly 17,400 notifications were received, compared to 13,500 in 2024. Something has happened there at a structural level that we have to work on and try to solve, says the general manager. Increases most among women The professional groups where workers take sick leave the most are welfare professions and public services. - It is about education, care and care. The biggest increases in reported occupational diseases this year are in the municipal sector, the care sector and most of all in certain housing support areas. Nursing homes and homes for care and accommodation, says Lars Lööw. This, in turn, can explain why the increase in sick leave is greatest among women, who accounted for seven out of ten notifications in 2025. - It may then be because the occupational groups in question are largely women who work in them. These are public services, care, care and education. There are most women there, quite simply, says Lars Lööw. The employer has the greatest responsibility The Work Environment Agency states that the issue is a major structural challenge, but that the greatest responsibility lies with the employer, primarily regions and municipalities.  - You need to think systematically and include work environment issues in the overall ones
de6c9880f1c2f975c3d8636eaa3a7fed1dc87081: The number of children born prematurely in Ukraine is increasing: "Acute stress"
dfadd4eec3ae61a87904bbbf57febc93102774ac:
Since Russia's invasion began in 2022, the fertility rate in Ukraine has fallen to among the lowest in the world. On average, a Ukrainian woman now gives birth to only one child.

At the same time, figures from the UN and new scientific studies show that a greater proportion of children born are premature. In some regions near the front lines, the number of premature births has doubled compared to pre-war times. Born at week 26: "Be terrified" Marharyta Nekhoroshyva lives in the hard-hit Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhya, near the southern front line. She gave birth to her child after only 26 weeks of pregnancy, and the son weighed 940 grams. She testifies about the great anxiety she felt during her pregnancy. - I was terrified when I heard explosions, really terrified. And when you are responsible for yourself and the little person inside you, it is even more terrifying. You have to be very careful, seek shelter and hide somewhere at night. It was very difficult and scary, she tells AP.

Her son Mark survived and is now nine months old. On the other hand, he has chronic breathing problems, which has led to frequent hospital visits where the flight alarms often go off and the risk of explosions is high. Link between stress and infections The link between stress in mothers and premature birth is complex, according to experts AP spoke with. But research indicates that long-term psychological stress, such as being in war for a long time, increases the risk of giving birth prematurely. In addition, the risk of infections during pregnancy is considered to be higher.

- Premature birth is greatly affected by infections. If you cannot get the appropriate diagnosis and treatment early, then the risk is higher that you will have a premature birth, says the doctor Andrew Weeks, professor of international maternity care at the University of Liverpool, to the AP.

It is not only premature births that are increasing in Ukraine. Even emergency caesarean sections and other complications do, according to the UN Population Fund.

Check the association's rules of procedure It is important to know what applies in your housing association. Over a thousand pensioners have collected price information on 42 goods in 736 stores across Sweden. The survey, which is usually carried out in the autumn, was moved this year to the spring to avoid traders lowering prices during the measurement week. The food box has become cheaper Earlier this year, the government halved the VAT on food. This year, PRO's food box has become cheaper, which is mainly explained by the reduced food VAT from 12 to 6 percent.  - Oranges and orange juice have become much cheaper. It's probably because there is a surplus and it didn't last time. All dairy products have also become cheaper. It's nice because it's something we need and it's due to overproduction in Europe, says Åsa Lindestam, chairman of PRO. The exception is, among other things, ground beef, which has become more expensive as a result of the shortage of the product.  Big differences between regions The result shows that Skåne is the cheapest, while Jämtland is the most expensive to shop in. According to Åsa Lindestam, this may be because Jämtland has more small shops, which often means higher prices.  Cross-border trade can also play a role, but PRO believes that the size of the stores is the biggest explanation for the price differences. PRO only measures regular prices, not extra prices, which means that basic goods can also greatly affect the result.  Advice to consumers Åsa Lindestam urges consumers to be price conscious and compare prices between different stores.  - Be price conscious and unfaithful. 8447603443612e7d7c6b1610f175ac194458b576: The Irish low-cost airline Ryanair is being investigated by Britain's competition authority after the company introduced a fee that parents are forced to pay to sit next to their children, reports Sky News. According to the airline's terms and conditions, parents must pay to sit next to children between the ages of two and eleven, who must sit with at least one of their parents. The fee is £8 per flight, corresponding to approximately SEK 100. May contravene the Consumer Protection Act The authority is investigating whether the fee may be about so-called "drip pricing", where mandatory fees are not immediately clear. It may run afoul of rules that require businesses to display a total price including all unavoidable charges, so consumers can compare prices and understand the true cost. At the same time, the authority states that the investigation is at an early stage and that the authority has not yet drawn any conclusions about whether the airline broke the law. Ryanair is the only major airline flying from Britain to impose such a fee, according to the country's competition authority. Calling the investigation a "scam" Ryanair describes the investigation as a "scam". "Like all adults who select a reserved seat, adults traveling with children pay a reserved seat fee, but can select reserved seats next to them for up to four children on the same booking free of charge," a Ryanair spokesperson told Sky News. How the investigation proceeds depends on what evidence comes to light, the competition authority states.

e08ccc99ca0c60eccbe04e2ac4e85e7c88e760f2:
What started with the storm Johannes now risks developing into a much bigger problem. When over eleven million cubic meters of forest were blown over during the winter, ideal conditions were simultaneously created for the spruce bark borer. The fallen firs act as a perfect nursery for the insect. There, the bark beetles can lay their eggs and develop undisturbed during the summer.  The Norwegian Forestry Agency follows developments closely in the hardest hit areas in Dalarna, Gävleborg and Västernorrland. Can spread to healthy forest The biggest concern is not the already fallen trees, but what happens next year. If the population of spruce bark beetles grows large enough, they can leave the windfalls and begin to attack living spruces.

- Weakened trees are what they attack in the first place. But if the population of the spruce bark beetle becomes too large, they will also venture into standing forest and try to reproduce there, says Magnus Martinsson.

Previous outbreaks have shown the consequences it can have. After the dry summers of 2018, large parts of the country were affected by extensive bark beetle damage. Since then, the losses for Swedish forest owners are estimated at around SEK 14 billion. The males come first On the storm-felled trees you can already see clear signs of activity. Small holes in the bark reveal that the first bark borers have arrived.

- It seems that only the males have arrived here yet. It's the males that burrow in and make a small chamber where they want to mate with the females, says Magnus Martinsson.

When the females are attracted to the tree, the next phase of the insects' life cycle begins. The larvae then develop under the bark before a new generation of bark borers leaves the tree later in the summer. The fir's defense is not always enough. Normally, the fir has its own defense against attacks. When the bark beetle burrows in, the tree tries to squeeze out resin to drown the insects. But weakened trees have a harder time resisting. And if many bark beetles attack at the same time, even healthy firs can give way.

ff809f19f3bbc0975ef0e422c76adb079eea38bd: The electricity companies' annual profit margin has been 16-23 percent in the years 2020-2024, shows a new report from the Energy Market Inspectorate (Ei). Over the past 20 years they have increased the electricity grid charge by 115 percent, more than double the rate of inflation of 49 percent. And small businesses have to pay a disproportionate amount. According to the organization Företagarna's calculations, based on data from Statistics Sweden, small businesses pay approximately 20 times more per kilowatt hour compared to the industrial giants. The Entrepreneurs: "Exploiting their monopoly position" André Nilsson, spokesperson for the Entrepreneurs, is critical of the power grid companies being able to make so much profit. - What stands out here is that small businesses have really become the power grid's cash cow, says Nilsson. - Small businesses somehow become the ones who have to pay the most, while at the same time they are the biggest taxpayers in nine out of ten municipalities and create the most new jobs. The report, says Nilsson, confirms the Entrepreneurs' view that the electricity grid companies have "exploited their monopoly position". - Profit margins of 16-23 percent in a regulated monopoly are remarkably high. "I don't notice any improvement - just get a higher price" Nilsson sees a couple of big problems with how the system works today. - The first is that it is really only Sweden and Finland within the EU where the network companies can set their own fees without a regulatory authority approving them in advance. It's a system error. He is also critical of new players not having to pay for the infrastructure required when they have to connect to the electricity grid. - Today, a florist in Svalöv participates and pays for parts of the infrastructure needed for a new data center in Sollefteå, when the cost is shared between everyone on the electricity grid. Then the fee increases even though they may not notice any improvement in the electricity grid they use - they just get a higher price. The current system makes it more difficult for small business owners to invest and grow, says André Nilsson. - It is a backwards system.

Taking the electric scooter to a friend or to the bar can feel like a convenient alternative in the summer heat. But it's not really that wonderful for everyone. At the beginning of June, the Swedish Transport Agency released new figures which now show the entire 2025 accident statistics with electric scooters. Last year, seven people died and 6,624 were injured. This is a sharp increase of 38 percent, compared to the year before. NTF monitors children's driving The National Traffic Safety Association, NTF, conducted a parent survey earlier this spring which showed that there is a knowledge gap regarding children's use of electric scooters. Now the organization follows up the results through checks where children under the age of 15 are observed, to see how reality matches the statistics. TV4 Nyheterna was present during a check in the Sturegatan-Karlavägen intersection at Östermalm in central Stockholm. For just under two hours in the afternoon traffic, we see several cases of dangerous behaviour. In some cases, it is also illegal. - When we are out and observe children on electric scooters, it is above all common to see that they do not use a helmet. You can also see that there are a lot of people driving and that is not allowed. The electric scooter is a vehicle that is made for one person and it is not legal to ride someone else on it, says Fiona Nicklin at NTF.

To make it simple, you should stick to the two-hour rule in summer heat for all refrigerated goods. In a normal room temperature of 20 degrees, four hours are valid, says Catarina Flink, microbiologist at the Swedish Food Agency. Smaller portions One tip is not to bring out all the midsummer food at once, but to bring it out in smaller portions and top up when needed. - When it's summer and hot outside, it's extra important to remember that food should be stored in a cool place, and that it's not in direct sunlight. It is also important to have good hand hygiene, use clean utensils and keep food clean. It reduces the risk of dangerous microorganisms spreading in the food, Catarina Flink continues. It is not possible to determine whether and, if so, which disease-causing microorganisms are present in the food. If the food is left out in the heat for too long, bacteria can grow and make people sick with, for example, stomach symptoms such as diarrhea and vomiting. - Another good tip is to make sure you have four degrees in the fridge because few bacteria can grow in such low temperatures, and thus the food lasts longer. Dangerous mold toxins Sometimes you can see that the food has gone bad, for example if it is discolored, slimy, has changed structure or if gas has formed in the packaging. Yeasts and molds are also usually clearly visible. The latter can form dangerous mold toxins. The ability to form mold toxins varies greatly between different types of mold. Some types do not form mold toxins at all. - In Sweden, it is very unusual for food to contain such high levels of mold toxins that we become acutely ill. But exposure to mold toxins for a long time can have serious health effects, for example liver and kidney damage as well as cancer, says Catarina Flink.

According to the indictment, the woman should not have received food, liquid or medicine. In the end, the son called 112 after the mother was unconscious and had not taken any liquid for at least two days. The news agency Siren was the first to report on it. - Hello. You, my mother, she had a stroke here a few days ago, says the son when the emergency operator answers the call. During the emergency call, he describes her condition as "something hovering between sleep and coma".  When the woman arrived at the emergency department, she was unconscious and dehydrated with acute kidney failure. She also had elevated infection values ​​and ulcers over the sacrum. She later died later in hospital. The son: "Euthanasia clinics" The medical assessment together with the forensic findings indicate that the cause of death was blood poisoning as a result of acute pneumonia. In questioning, the son has said that he promised his father that the mother would die at home and not in hospital, and that he therefore did not alert the medical service immediately. "There are no hospitals, it's euthanasia clinics," the son said in questioning. The son also claims that "there was no ambulance that came, but an ambulance whose staff euthanized her as soon as they had loaded her." Suspected of causing her death The prosecutor believes that the son left her sick without treatment, did not call an ambulance despite clear symptoms and left her lying there for several days - and thereby caused the death. The woman's relatives had previously raised the alarm that the man could be dangerous to his mother and that he prevented contact with the mother. The man denies wrongdoing. - Fiction, a fairy tale. I deny it, the man replies when asked how he reacts to the suspicions.

First picture Now TV4 Nyheterna can show the first picture of Mette-Marit from inside the hospital. Then you are in the intensive care unit for two to three days and then in the ward for two to three weeks, he says. - She is probably still in intensive care and may go from there to the intensive care unit in a day or so, continues the chief physician. The Crown Princess was diagnosed in 2018 with the chronic disease pulmonary fibrosis.  During the spring, the disease worsened and the doctors judged that a transplant was necessary, whereupon she was put on the waiting list. Even then, her doctors were clear that Mette-Marit would not have any priority in the gender.  But it did not take many days before the transplant was completed.
