At the Gesundbrunnen train station in northern Berlin there is a small white house. If you unlock the door and go in, there is a staircase there. If you follow it, you will come to the German capital's only shelter. And it's not impressive.  Around 900 people can fit. In the largest room there are some wooden benches. In another room there is a stack of folding chairs and cans for water.  The funding was withdrawn. The shelter was built in the 1920s and was used extensively during the Second World War. After the war, it and other similar shelters were maintained in West Berlin. The threat from East Germany and the Soviet Union was palpable for decades. However, with the fall of the Berlin Wall, political interest in the shelters disappeared, and in the mid-2000s, funding was completely withdrawn for all shelters throughout the country.  This very thing was preserved as a museum object, and the organization Berlins Underjord makes small guided walks through the facility. And should there be a crisis or a war, the organization will open the shelter to the public.  But for a city of 3.8 million people, Berlin's only preserved shelter is of course a drop in the ocean.  The government wants to invest All around Germany it looks the same. A few shelters have been preserved for nostalgic reasons and some private individuals have built their own bunkers. But in the event of a war or a crisis, there is only room for less than one percent of the population.  The German government has now put forward a proposal to clean up shelters and build new ones and will soon release an app that shows the nearest place where people can seek shelter in a crisis. The concern that Kay Heyne has is that too many resources are being put into the app and not enough into the shelters.  - Right now the app would only show that there are no shelters at all, he says and laughs.

f4a0abb17a0e624c9620538c0b5e30d951fd0296: As the whole Earth warms, there is an exception. Just south of Iceland and Greenland, a small part of the Atlantic Ocean is an area that is getting colder and colder. It is called the cold blob. The Swedish ocean climate scientist Léon Chafik has worked with the spot for a long time. - When the whole world warms up over a long period of time, there is a hole, the cold spot, he explains. The new study: Happening deep down Before some people thought that the cold spot was only on the surface of the water, but a new German study suggests that the cooling also takes place deep down in the water. It could indicate that the gulf stream system, the system of underwater currents that make the winters in Scandinavia milder than in Canada or Alaska, among others, is weakening. The scientific community expects the system to become weaker until the year 2100. This is because there is more fresh water at higher latitudes, which in turn is due to more precipitation and melting ice. After an examination, the cancer was found, he says.  The illness notice turned life completely upside down. - I thought, well, I'm going to die now. It was a big shock and I barely remembered anything from when I got the news about the disease, says Rickard Fredlund. More and more are affected Every year approximately 7,500 people in Sweden are affected by colon and rectal cancer.  From 2022, everyone between the ages of 60 and 74 will be called to screening, a sample, in order to detect this cancer at an early stage. But recent statistics show that participation in bowel cancer screening among men in northern Sweden in particular is low - almost 4 out of 10 men in the northern parts of the country neglect to take the test. - It is difficult to explain exactly why it looks like this. But in general it can be said that men in northern Sweden care less about their health than in the rest of the country, says Olof Sjöström, chief surgeon at Östersund Hospital and member of the national working group for colon and rectal cancer screening.  Then the chances are good. The screening consists of a test that you do at home on your own by collecting a stool sample which is then sent for analysis. If the sample shows signs of, for example, blood, you will be called to the healthcare system for a bowel examination.  - If we find the disease in what we call stage one, i.e. early, then nine out of ten survive. If the cancer has time to spread, it may be too late so nothing can be done, says chief physician Olof Sjöström. After radiation, chemotherapy and surgery, Rickard Fredlund finally managed to get rid of his cancer. But he still goes for checks and still doesn't dare to exhale completely. He urges everyone who gets the opportunity to undergo the screening to detect the cancer in time. - I think it is extremely important, it can be completely life-changing, he says.

Don't stress buy Mascara, sunscreen and shampoo are also often significantly more expensive at the airport. - You often see the slightly more luxurious brands and think that they are good offers, but that is not the case. It is wise to pack from home instead of stress buying at the airport, says Isabella Ahmadi.  Bargains can be made - but require checking There are, however, exceptions. Two out of ten products are cheaper at duty-free than online. The majority of products are more expensive in duty free shops there too. - You must always be aware of the price, says Ahmadi. According to Marie-Louise Danielsson-Tham, professor of food hygiene, mistakes are made that can easily be avoided. - The most common mistake is forgetting that food has to go into the fridge even faster than usual when it's hot. Everything thaws very quickly, even frozen food, she says. Many also leave the refrigerator door open for too long. - When it's hot, hot air flows quickly into the fridge. Then the food in the refrigerator quickly warms up. You may need to lower the temperature extra in the fridge, she says. "Cold, cold, cold" You have to think already in the grocery store. - Be prepared: load the cool bag when you shop and have extra cold packs. Put both at the bottom and on top of what you have bought, she says and adds: - Also try to park in the shade, even if it can be difficult. Think cold, cold, cold. She explains how most foods contain small amounts of bacteria, which in small amounts are not dangerous but multiply quickly in heat. - Then the durability deteriorates enormously, especially when it is also humid, says Danielsson-Tham. How to serve the food Warmth and holidays often lead to the grill coming out. Then it is important not to have sauces and the like on the table for too long. - The food quickly ends up at a temperature where bacteria thrive. Then it becomes bad and dangerous much faster. Also, it's not very pleasant to eat lukewarm food. I think you should keep the food inside and quickly put it back in the fridge, she says. The advice is clear: - It is better to take it out again when you want to take more. If the food is left out for too long, bacteria can multiply. - Bacteria such as staphylococci can form toxins in food. You can get really sick with symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea, headaches. You feel very bad, but often it passes quite quickly, says Danielsson-Tham. How long can the food be kept?

Employees suffered from symptoms such as irritated airways, severe headaches, nosebleeds and vomiting. One had chemically induced airway inflammation, which occurs when people inhale chemicals. But the company believes that a combination of fine dust, weather and a respiratory virus was behind the incidents. The experts do not agree Now an examination from Dagens Nyheter shows that SSAB's own experts do not agree with the official explanation. When the newspaper talks to one of the experts that SSAB used to reach the conclusion, virus researcher Niklas Arnberg at Umeå University, he says that there is not enough evidence to say that a respiratory virus was behind the incidents. When asked if it could have been due to dangerous gases or dust particles, he replies that it cannot be ruled out. - But I didn't get any questions about it, says Arnberg to DN. SSAB: Safe with our conclusions Occupational and environmental medicine in the north at Norrland University Hospital in Umeå, which the company also used, does not believe that respiratory tract infections are a satisfactory explanation either. And that it would be about fine-grained dust seems "experientially very unlikely", they write to DN. When DN talks to a number of other researchers in work environment medicine, they are all critical of SSAB's explanation. - It feels like this was the easy way out, that it would be the only explanation, says Maria Kippler, lecturer and associate professor at KI, to the newspaper. SSAB writes to DN that they feel safe with their conclusions. However, they do not answer the question if they are completely confident that new cases of the disease will not occur.

The police can test AI facial recognition - with pictures of you The police can start using images of individuals filmed by the general camera surveillance. 42-year-old Mikael Johnsson is Öland's youngest professional fisherman. Like his father and grandfather, he lives on what the sea has to offer, but with reduced fishing quotas and a regulatory framework he describes as complicated, it has become more difficult.

Last year, a trial ban was introduced against coastal trawl fishing in parts of the central Baltic Sea. Mikael Johnsson thought that small trawlers like his Solana would be exempted, but that was not the case. The ban has meant that he and other fishermen have to look for new areas.  The trawl ban affects everyday life - We have had to look for other areas and it has resulted in new good fishing waters for all intents and purposes, but it takes a lot more fuel for us and we have to go far to find the fish. It has made life much more difficult for us.

The trawl ban was introduced to give the endangered stock of sturgeon a chance to recover. What happens after the trial period, which runs until April next year, remains unclear.

Minister of Rural Affairs Peter Kullgren writes in a comment to TV4 Nyheterna that the government wants to permanently move the trawl limit for large-scale trawl fishing along the entire Swedish Baltic Sea coast. Small-scale fishermen are therefore not to be covered by a new regulation.  Started food truck Mikael Johnsson still takes nothing for granted. In addition to refining his catch, this year he started a food truck to get more legs to stand on. In order to break the trend, where the professional fishermen on Öland have decreased in two decades from around 50 to today's 10, he believes that a change in attitude is required.

- Yes, first there must be a belief in the future and today there is so much negative talk about fishing. We would like to see a more positive image of fishing and of course there needs to be regulation, but it is not small vessels that threaten a stock. Bigger withdrawals make a bigger impact - it's simple math, he concludes.

New study A new study from the Karolinska Institutet and the Public Dental Service has compared how white and brown snus affects oral health.  Thickening of the mucous membrane affects both, but white snus also causes inflammation and sores in the mouth that did not occur when using brown snus.

Some tastes worse The study is the first in the world to compare oral health between users of white and brown snus. The researchers were surprised by the fact that the inflammation that occurred with white snus was not affected by how much one snused, but instead a connection was seen with the flavoring of the snus.

- There is a clear trend towards the slightly more inflammatory reactions and ulcers that you see with white snus being linked to mint flavors and menthol, says Lars Fredriksson.

Elin Dahlgren from Gothenburg has recently stopped snus but still has a tin of mint-flavored white snus at home and does not rule out that she will pick up the habit again. The fact that mint can be more harmful than other flavors wouldn't make her want to switch.

Now, researchers at Chalmers in Gothenburg and at the Swedish Transport Administration have analyzed all 204 fatal accidents involving e-scooters, e-bikes and regular bicycles in Sweden between 2016 and 2024. The e-scooters stand out both in terms of drivers and accident patterns. It may seem like we are comparing vehicles. But in practice we are comparing people. There are different populations and different uses of the vehicles, says Marco Dozza, who is professor of active safety and road user behavior at Chalmers. Private scooters Some of the results are relatively expected, he notes. This applies, for example, to the fact that the use of helmets among those who died was very low, regardless of vehicle type. A little more unexpected, however, was that the fatal accidents with electric scooters stand out in terms of the percentage of drivers under the influence of alcohol. In addition, it turned out that most of the fatal accidents occurred with privately owned e-scooters - while the public debate was largely about the rental e-scooters. Since there are so many that are rented out, we thought that the statistics would show that more people die on a rented electric scooter. But it was the other way around, says Marco Dozza. Lack of standards In order to reverse the trend, more regulation is not needed in the first place, he believes. Instead, it is about changing the approach to the electric scooter as a vehicle. Today, there are few established social norms around electric scooters, as they are still relatively new. They are therefore often perceived more as toys than as real vehicles, he says. But I think we need to start looking at e-scooters the same way we look at bicycles. For example, parents teaching their children to ride an electric scooter and making sure they wear a helmet, even when riding an electric scooter.

You get the best effect if you mash the common garden plant before spreading it around you. But it's not because the leaves smell bad that mosquitoes run away. According to Marcus Stensmyr, docent in biology at Lund University, substances in the catnip activate pain receptors in mosquitoes that are normally triggered by high temperatures.  - So when mosquitoes come near catnip, they probably experience severe pain, he tells TV4 Nyheterna. If you want to use catnip as a mosquito repellent, it can be smart to plant it in a pot or in a flower bed where it will not take over, as it can spread quickly. - If you don't have it at home, a neighbor probably has it, he says. More plants can keep mosquitoes away Catnip is not the only plant that can repel mosquitoes. Several aromatic herbs can also help, such as basil, rosemary, lemon balm and lavender. - Lemon balm probably works somewhat in the same way, that it also activates pain receptors like this, says Marcus Stensmyr. He advises growing several varieties near the patio and placing pots on the table when you sit and eat. - Not adequate protection, as if you had a lot of mosquito repellent, but it helps. Catnip also attracts a lot of bumblebees and butterflies. - It looks nice, you can eat it and it also keeps away mosquitoes and gnats and other things. That's why it's called catmint. The name comes from the fact that some cats react strongly when they come into contact with the plant. According to Marcus Stensmyr, the effect can be extra strong in sexually mature cats. - It can produce some kind of very strange, almost narcotic and erotic effect. It lasts about a quarter of an hour, maybe 20 minutes, and then it's over, he says.

Exactly why cats like catnip is still unclear. But it is known that fleas, ticks and other things that the cat does not want on it can be scared away by the smell.

- There have been suggestions that cats like it precisely because they rub themselves in catnip and thus use it as a mosquito repellent.

"Fantastic" The announcement comes after the regions' expert council, the NT Council, updated its recommendations and opened the way for the medicine to be offered to patients who meet special criteria. - There were quite high criteria and it was unclear whether Anna would fulfill them. But after going through her case, it has now been established that she meets the requirements set, says Christoffer Eriksson. The family no longer needs to raise money for the treatment, as it is now financed within Swedish healthcare. Anna can also receive her treatment at Sunderby Hospital, just 15 minutes from home, instead of having to make four-day trips to Germany.  - It is fantastic. It is great and happy news, he says. Paid 250,000 a month When the couple visited Nyhetsmorgon in April this year, Christoffer told that Anna loses bodily functions for every day that goes by without the medicine. When she started the treatment, the hope was that it would eventually be able to continue in Sweden. - To continue to self-finance a drug treatment that costs around a quarter of a million kroner a month - that is not sustainable. So this means a lot, he says. At the same time, Christoffer thinks it is fantastic that, thanks to support from the public, they were able to start the treatment even before the drug was recommended in Sweden. - This gives even more reasons to feel hope and confidence in the future. Anna is expected to receive the first treatment in Sweden in August.

Milly's adventure began with an idea to do something challenging, something Nya Wermlands-Tidningen has written about before. 

Together with father Marco and his uncle, they climbed Kebnekaise, which is 2096.8 meters above sea level, via the eastern route. It is a route that is both longer and more technically demanding than the classic route.

9bb6071f39a8227404879040cf2a978cf3491825: The summer baby boom: This is why most babies are born in July
8014f28c892c2919c7e4583061ad7e51fa6f8185: It is no coincidence that little Julian celebrates his 1st birthday on a July day. Mother Matilda lists several reasons why she wanted a summer child: - Everything is so much easier during the summer. You go on holiday, parental leave during the summer - much nicer than going in November, for example. You can time the leave with each other. Summer parties are cozier. It's nicer to be heavily pregnant in the summer, in my opinion, with clothes and such.  Most common days to be born on During 2025, an average of 292 children were born per day in July – to compare with December, when the fewest children were born: 225 per day. The top three most common days to be born on were July 3, July 14 and June 12, according to Statistics Norway. But it hasn't always looked like this. Previously, the biggest birth boom occurred in the spring, in March and April. - So nine months after midsummer and the industrial holiday. And even earlier, when Sweden was still a farming society, most people were born in September and October, i.e. nine months after the Christmas holiday, explains Lena Lundkvist, demographer at Statistics Norway. Increased planning is probably behind The change with more and more summer children began to be seen around the turn of the millennium and the reason behind it is believed to be increased and conscious family planning. - The mother and father want to be off together in the summer, have a little longer leave then. But it's hard to know. You might also plan for there to be available kindergarten places, says Lena Lundkvist. Something that Matilda Blom and her partner sign up to. Because despite the fact that they noticed that summer is the most stressful time for maternity care - it was full in labor and delivery when Julian was born on that July day - they would invest in another summer baby in the event of another sibling attempt. - I myself am a January child, my partner was born in December, so we are done with winter. Now we focus on summer birthdays, says Matilda Blom.

However, one should always be skeptical of unexpected content such as requests for money transfers, transfer of sensitive information or disclosure of passwords or user details. a012e49243cc756acd4799f957e175e22d8fe2d9:
Måns Lagmark was a valued soccer goalkeeper and a person who was always there for others. But behind the cheerful facade, he struggled for over ten years with mental illness and autism, a struggle that worsened when the school's routines disappeared.

- He was the kindest person in the world. There is not a single person who has anything bad to say about him, says sister Maja Lagmark. "He was let down" Despite Måns repeatedly asking for help, he never got the support he needed. According to Maja, he was bounced between different parts of the care, without anyone taking overall responsibility. - He was enrolled in adult psychiatry. They blamed the habilitation. No one took responsibility. We got no help, she says. Suicide expert Ulla-Karin Nyberg believes that the story reflects a larger problem. - To bounce a person between different agencies when what is needed is cooperation and security is a system error. We are organized in a way that doesn't work for these people. "How sick do you have to be to get help?" After the brother's death, grief has been mixed with guilt and questions about everything that could have been done differently. - You put a lot of blame on yourself after an event like this. But I said all those things that you think: "If only I said it one more time." He knew I loved him, says Maja. Ulla-Karin Nyberg emphasizes that relatives must become a natural part of care. - We have to cooperate with relatives and relatives. They are the only ones who know how changed the person is. You cannot see that in a single meeting. Want Mån's story to make a difference Today, Maja chooses to openly talk about her brother's death in the hope that other families will not have to go through the same thing. - No one is taken seriously. A lot of people say the same thing. If I can make a difference for someone else, it's worth it, she says. Ulla-Karin Nyberg calls for more coordination and greater resources within psychiatry. - Mental illness can be a life-threatening condition. We must treat it with the same seriousness as other life-threatening diseases.

The fraudster said that she might have been cheated on her bank ID or that someone was shopping in her name and therefore the invoice would be paused. - He then asked which bank I had and if I had a banker. And when I replied that I didn't have it, he connected me to my bank, she says.
Approved fake invoices A long conversation took place in which the man said he was from Sofia's bank and said that someone had come across her bank ID, but in fact it was about her being the victim of a fraud at that moment. - When I tell you this, I feel like it's a "Red Flag", but I didn't connect at the time, she says. According to the Wall Street Journal, tramadol is sold in the Central African Republic in the form of high-dose tablets, well above the recommended level. Miners during gold extraction are said to use it to cope with long shifts. Demonstrators take it to quell hunger and fatigue, and combatants use it to become more aggressive and less fearful. "In combat situations, tramadol is used in huge doses," says Nathalia Dukhan, a researcher at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, a think tank based in Geneva. "Fear disappears and anxiety increases when combatants are put into a pharmacological trance." Taken control of the state According to information provided to the Wall Street Journal, the network's influence has become so extensive that tramadol is not only distributed among local militias and combatants, but is also said to be delivered to members of the elite force that makes up the president's bodyguard. The same source says supplies also go to an influential youth militia in Bangui known as the "Sharks", known for armed patrols in the capital and for harassing and beating opposition supporters. The group's control of the tramadol trade also helps them exploit timber and gold resources The Wagner group has effectively taken control of the state, according to the Africa Center for Strategic Studies, which is supported by the Pentagon, writes the Wall Street Journal. After calling 1177, she was sent to the emergency room where the doctors first suspected a heart attack. But the examinations showed that the coronary arteries of the heart were free of narrowings. Instead, she was diagnosed with Takotsubo – then a relatively unknown heart disease. 

- They were absolutely sure it was a heart attack. But when they saw my heart and everything, no, there were no strictures. So it wasn't a heart attack, says Anna-Lena Brundin.  Stress can be a triggering factor Both times Anna-Lena was affected, she had been unusually nervous before a performance. Afterwards, the symptoms came when she was in the car on the way home.

- Very strange, she says. Takutsubo, first described in Japan in the 1990s, is an acute condition in which the heart temporarily weakens, often after a severe stress attack. The symptoms are almost identical to heart attacks, and the disease mainly affects women between the ages of 60 and 80. - The cause is a sharp increase in stress hormones in the body, typically adrenaline, says Daniel Lindholm, cardiologist and heart researcher.  Can be life-threatening Most people make a full recovery, but in the acute phase the condition can be serious.

- We have a mortality of around five percent in the first month, says Daniel Lindholm. 

Anna-Lena now tries to avoid stress in order to reduce the risk of being affected again.  - I've always thought I'm very cool, and not so sensitive in that way, but apparently I am, she says. 

Research into Takutsubo continues and healthcare has become better at recognizing and treating the condition. But much is still unknown about why some are affected.

Affects the body and brain Sweden is a country that is built for cold, and in everyday life heat is often seen as something positive. At Lund University, research is being done on how people react in really hot environments. There is a climate chamber that can simulate a heat wave. You also have more difficulty concentrating and making decisions, says Clara Heil, who is a doctoral student in ergonomics and aerosol technology at Lund University and researches how heat affects us humans. Trees and social cohesion can reduce the risks The advice to cope with a heat wave is described as simple but important: shield yourself from the sun, ventilate when it's cooler outside, drink water, avoid exertion in the middle of the day and keep an eye on the indoor temperature.

To protect a city, more greenery is also highlighted. Trees lower the temperature by providing shade, but also through their cellular respiration where they transpire water that cools the surroundings, says Emanuel Toft, climate adaptation strategist at the Environmental Administration in Malmö city. There are studies that show that in areas where social cohesion is perceived to be stronger, the health outcome during a heat wave is milder.

030657a1a7721baf70451b9e0324d14e726537ab: This is how you best master the stomach bug: "It's number one"
68e36c34965aa459d6af134fde0a9419defeeb4b: According to Robel Malki, there are four common causes of stomach upset: tourist's diarrhea, food poisoning, stomach flu and parasites.  The most common is tourist's diarrhea. Symptoms usually appear after one to three days and last for a few days. But there are several ways to reduce the risk of the holiday being spent in the hotel toilet.  - Good hand hygiene, that's number one. Avoid tap water, peel fruit and perhaps avoid ice in the drink, says Robel Malki.  During the summer, food buffets and all inclusive can attract many vacationers. But the buffets can also become a breeding ground for bacteria and cause food poisoning. - Then the bacteria can release poisons, toxins, which remain alive in the food even though the bacteria have died. You get symptoms in the form of vomiting within 1-6 hours. And if you're extra lucky, you'll also get diarrhoea, says Robel Malki.  "Very contagious" Stomach flu is not as common in summer as in winter, but it can occur, says Robel Malki. - It is viruses that cause it, very contagious between people. But also passes within 24 to 48 hours, sometimes a little longer, says Robel Malki.  Parasites are less common, but can cause long-term problems. The symptoms can only appear after several weeks and the diarrhea can last for a long time.  - If you are in India, for example, and you happen to get parasites via water or other means, you don't feel anything initially. You come home and after one to two weeks you start to have foul-smelling, watery diarrhea and so you don't really connect that it has to do with abroad, says Robel Malki.  Dehydration The most important thing with stomach flu is to get enough fluid, because the body loses large amounts of fluid and salts through vomiting and diarrhea.  - If you think fluid replacement is disgusting, you can drink broth and water instead. Many people ask about juice and soft drinks, but this should be avoided because they contain a lot of sugar, which can worsen the diarrhea, says Robel Malki. Then you should seek care to avoid dehydration
b9b148861e41b96003c0795d92df0f9ba7ca333f: Study: Only girls get anxiety from nicotine - boys become depressed
5c4c829e49de0cd8396861b0bd452e7c192a0be5: Young people who use nicotine experience symptoms of anxiety, depression and mental illness more often than peers who do not use nicotine, studies from the University of Gothenburg show.  By following young people over a longer period, the researchers were able to see that so-called psychosomatic symptoms such as stomach aches, headaches and sleep problems increased when the young people started using nicotine. The symptoms increase both when using traditional tobacco products and tobacco-free nicotine products such as white snus and e-cigarettes.  Louise Adermark is a professor at Sahlgrenska Academy, Gothenburg University, and one of the research leaders behind the studies: - Those who never start with nicotine have quite low levels and those who start with nicotine have low levels before they start. So it is in connection with starting to use nicotine that we see these symptoms increase, she says.  Girls are more affected In one of the studies, about 80 percent of the girls who used nicotine reported what the researchers call "clinically relevant anxiety symptoms." - We only saw the anxiety symptoms in girls, but on the other hand we saw that depressive symptoms also became more common among the boys, says Louise Adermark.  She explains that there are many factors that can contribute to the result.  - It could be that nicotine actually affects the brain a little differently and you don't really know why, but it could be linked to sex hormones, for example. It may also be linked to how the brain is interconnected in general. There are big differences between girls and boys in how they deal with stress and things like that, she says.  By studying how the rats' brains react to nicotine, the researchers could see that the amygdala brain area, which is important for emotion regulation and stress, was most affected in the females. - We cannot say with one hundred percent certainty, but we see that there is a connection between nicotine exposure and an effect on the brain. And we think that the female brain is perhaps more vulnerable, says Louise Aderma

923021871952b6e262289044b781acc64950cc40: For many, the summer means much-needed time off and time for fun, but also a risk that the holiday fund will quickly run out. Everyday economist Magnus Hjelmér believes that small expenses can be an expensive surprise when everyday life returns. - It's the smaller things that pull away, like when we're at the beach and buying ice cream, says Hjelmér. Planning important for the economy According to Magnus Hjelmér, it is common to want to treat yourself a little extra during the holidays, but that many forget to plan for the increased expenses. It is rarely the big costs, such as accommodation and travel, that cause it because most people have already saved for these. Instead, it is the small, spontaneous purchases – such as ice cream, coffee and entrance tickets – that can quickly become a heavy burden on the private economy. - It sticks out when it is not needed. It can be more expensive than you can imagine, says Hjelmér. He believes that many households rarely save for the summer, in the same way that there is often a lack of a Christmas budget. When the holidays do come, a buffer is therefore often missing and expenses can easily be higher than planned. Many hope that the holiday pay will cover the costs, but when the small purchases are added up, the total is often unexpectedly high. This is how much you can save. A typical day at the beach, in the park or in the forest, where a family of four buys food, drinks, ice cream and coffee on site, can cost around SEK 600-650. If the same family instead brings a packed lunch and coffee from home, the cost will be around SEK 230. - What happens if we are at the beach ten times? Then it is 4,000 bucks. It will be a lot of money, says Hjelmér. He points out that small price differences quickly grow into large amounts. An ice cream from the kiosk can cost SEK 20, while the same ice cream in a multipack from the store can cost SEK eight. 7968021f069c9ce56cfb3e89c4503262d4abb285: The call to Swedes: Be vigilant about fake banknotes
3eae1af16e5b3e4440833e8d14aa5eb4034f7be5:
Sweden's banknotes and coins are issued by the Riksbank. Statistics show that the number of counterfeit banknotes detected has varied in recent years. After the peak in 2020, the number has decreased, but fakes are still detected every year. 
The organization Swedish Trade receives about a handful of reports a week via its security center.

- Few people use cash. It is difficult to get an idea of ​​how many are counterfeit. But for us, the notifications we receive, we still receive a handful every week, says Nina Jelver, head of security at Swedish Trade. At the same time, the Riksbank emphasizes that the Swedish banknotes have strong protection against counterfeiting.

- Our notes are extremely secure. They are practically impossible to copy. But you can make them very similar to a real banknote, says Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen. According to Swedish Trade, the reduced use of cash has meant that fewer people recognize a genuine banknote. It is exploited by fraudsters, who often try to exchange a fake 500 note for smaller denominations or buy a cheap item to get genuine change back. The problem increases during the summer, when there are many summer workers with less experience in recognizing counterfeit notes manning the tills.

The most common sign of a counterfeit 500 note is that it is missing one of the note's security features. When the banknote is angled, the symbol should change from a crown to the letters "KR". It is an effect that is often missing on the copies.

Anyone who discovers a counterfeit note should, if possible, keep it and file a police report. The note must be saved because the police may need to confiscate it.

At the same time, the governor of the Riksbank believes that the security of the Swedish banknotes stands up well internationally.

- Very, very good. But we have the absolute highest standard you can have and of course we should have that, says Erik Thedéen.

2083198fd15e4c854d4f888bee1d348a1f501b5d: Five cups of coffee a day can reduce the risk of cancer
4f7f04a876c0115f1058f63caf297f090f6c88c3: That coffee has beneficial effects on health has been shown in several studies. Coffee drinking is linked to, among other things, a reduced risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and stroke. Now researchers at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles have investigated the possible effects of coffee on the liver. They analyzed data from about 355,000 people who were followed for about 13 years. Their conclusion: Drinking five cups of coffee or more a day can be linked to a 47 percent lower risk of developing liver cancer and a 32 percent lower risk of developing liver cirrhosis, also known as cirrhosis. The positive effects were seen for coffee both with and without caffeine. Sweetening the coffee with sugar or sweeteners only slightly reduced the healthy effects on the liver, according to the study published in the journal Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. Those who sweetened the coffee, on the other hand, had higher values ​​for a marker that can indicate inflammation and fibrosis in the liver, says Hyunseok Kim, transplant physician and one of the study authors, to CNN. Since even decaffeinated coffee appears to benefit the liver, researchers believe that the healthy effects come from the beverage's antioxidant properties. The researchers point out that the study participants were mainly of European descent and "relatively health conscious", which may have influenced the results.

7ebbb0aea04e932f4a158c09bfd3b6953e0f9faa: Some Copenhageners have curiously come to Amager to look at the famous caterpillar. They want to know how "difficult" it really is before they make an informed decision about how close "you really dare to go" to an image. You have to keep your distance without protective equipment, says Tonni Donovan to the young couple. But as long as it's not windy, you can go quite close. The oak processionary spinner - or the "caterpillar from hell" as it has come to be called in the Danish media, referring to its hairs which can cause intense itching and strong allergic reactions. The butterflies they give rise to can both fly and travel with the wind. Spread via oak trees In Denmark, experts believe that it has mainly spread via purchased oak trees. It was first found on the island of Funen in 2024, which has resulted in both closed schools and crisis meetings. At the same time, there is a debate going on about how dangerous it really is because other countries have lived with it for a long time. It's a bit like the killer snail. It doesn't kill, but this caterpillar is not very nice. Although the media have probably embellished the wording a bit, I understand that they want it removed, says Donovan. Last week there was an alarm that it had been found on three oaks on the island of Amager in the Danish capital, the number was quickly adjusted up to ten, then to 40 and now it is clear that it is about 90 trees. It's not something you can get rid of in the blink of an eye. We expect it to take two to three weeks, says Donovan, who is standing in full protective gear in a 30-degree Copenhagen. The company Rentokil has been commissioned by the municipality of Copenhagen to vacuum up all the larvae and then burn them. We hope to catch them all, but there is always the risk that some have hidden somewhere we haven't seen. A matter of time In Sweden, Didrik Vanhoenacker, biologist at the National Museum of Natural History, believes that it is only a matter of time before it crosses the strait. e10443c78e27b3b047e8cf2608f3b530661e48b0: It is researchers in Spain who have discovered sugar molecules through spectroscopy, which measures different wavelengths of light. The sugar they discovered is called erytrulose and is found in, among other things, raspberries and, somewhat unexpectedly, in tan-without-sunscreen. It is not the first time that scientists have discovered sugar molecules in space, but when it is in the gas clouds near the center of the Milky Way, where stars and planets can form, it becomes interesting, according to the scientists. This indicates that the sugar occurs spontaneously in the gas cloud. According to the researchers, erythrulose is one of the largest sugar molecules discovered so far. In addition to providing energy for various forms of life, sugar is an important component of life's building blocks, RNA and DNA. It may have come to Earth through a meteorite or comet that hit the Earth and be a clue to where the building blocks of life come from, Rebecca Allen of Swinburne University of Technology in Australia, who was not involved in the study, told NBC. The study has been published in the journal Nature Astronomy, and the researchers write that even if the newly discovered form of sugar is not essential for life, it may have played a role in starting life on Earth.

He also dispels the myth that testosterone use would contribute to increased aggression. - There are no studies that show that testosterone makes you aggressive. But among reed beds and in shallow water in the northern bay, work is currently underway to map where the pike spawn and grow up. With nets and other equipment, researchers and marine biologists search for newly hatched pike fry. - What we want to do in the project is to map where the game succeeds. Where do pike fry hatch? says Anniina Saarinen, marine biologist and project manager at the Västerbotten County Administrative Board. The small fry are only a few centimeters long, but can provide important knowledge about which coastal environments act as nurseries for fish. - We found a lot of fry here now, so absolutely - this really feels like a nursery, she says. Rivers meet seas The work is part of the HIDDEN project, which is run by Swedish and Finnish authorities and financed by the EU through Interreg Aurora. The project has a total budget of 2.49 million euros. The focus is on so-called estuaries, areas where rivers meet the sea and where fresh and salt water mix. These are environments that are important for fish, underwater plants and birds, but which are also sensitive to impact. Should help authorities protect areas Runoff from forestry, agriculture and industry affects the water. At the same time, dredging, jetties and other exploitation can change important habitats along the coast. Therefore, the project will map species, vegetation and seabeds. - It is important that we know where there are valuable areas, so that we can steer clear of harmful activities, says Anniina Saarinen. "Worth preserving" During the summer, mapping continues along several estuaries along the Norrland coast, both above and below the water surface. - In a bay like this, you wouldn't want to start dredging or building lots of piers and jetties when you know that it seems to be a great playground for the pike. Refrigerated goods such as milk, meat and fish are most affected by heat. While high humidity can cause mold growth on dry foods such as bread, and on fruit and vegetables. Promotes mold growth Therefore, it is important to store berries, fruit and vegetables in the refrigerator. The bread should be kept as dry as possible, preferably in the freezer and preferably packaged in portions. The vegetables and fruit can be dried from time to time because moisture favors mold growth even in the refrigerator, continues Ellen Edgren. Simple rules are that hot food must be kept warm and cold food cold. Not leaving refrigerated goods outside in summer heat for longer than two hours. And to ensure that the refrigerator maintains a temperature of four degrees. Before placing hot food in the refrigerator, it should be cooled down quickly. Cooler lamps can also be used when transporting refrigerated goods home from the store - if you don't have a cooler bag handy, advises Ellen Edgren. Microorganisms, especially bacteria, grow rapidly on fresh products such as milk, fish, meat, chicken and shellfish. Lactic acid bacteria that are naturally present in milk cause the milk to sour when it is warm. Listeria bacteria are sometimes found in fish, mainly in raw and smoked fish. Listeria can cause fever, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea. Pregnant women, the elderly and people with weakened immune systems are extra sensitive to listeria. Keep an eye on hygiene Chicken often carries the bacterium campylobacter. Therefore, you should always cook chicken thoroughly, and be careful with hygiene when handling raw chicken meat, Edgren points out. All bacteria disappear when the food is cooked through. Response within two days The suspected skin change is photographed at the health center and sent for analysis to a group of specialist doctors at Karolinska University Hospital who, after a collective assessment, can provide an initial diagnosis. 

- Often we have been able to give an answer within two days, it almost never takes longer than a week, says Niki Radros, specialist in dermatology at Karolinska University Hospital.

But in the rearview mirror, we see that it backfires like a boomerang against American households and businesses. According to Bergqvist, studies show that around 90 percent of the increased customs costs have been borne by American companies – that is, importers in the US who pay the duties – and by extension by American consumers. The result has been classic Swedish summer weather with variable cloudiness and recurring showers. Showers and windy during the weekend The weather is expected to continue to be unstable in the near future. During the weekend, new showers move in across the country and temperatures will stay around 15-20 degrees. - We'll probably have to drag this coolness a little longer. It will be showers and windy this weekend, says Johan Wiksten. However, the unstable weather with both low and high pressure is not unusual for Sweden during the summer. - We should not have high pressure and 30 degrees for four weeks. It is not normal, but that we have a little mixed compote is normal, he explains.  The heat returns in the middle of next week Those who yearn for higher temperatures will instead have to wait a few days into next week. The forecasts show that warmer winds may begin to move in as early as Wednesday.  Then it will be southern Sweden and above all the Baltic Sea coast that will get the warmest.  - From the middle of the week and through the week, we get high pressure in southern Sweden. The Baltic Sea landscape can certainly get up to around 25 degrees, says Johan Wiksten.

Residues of medicines can get further into nature and end up in the bodies of wild animals. Now a study from Sweden's Agricultural University, SLU, shows that more than half of 152 rats examined in Brazil carried antibiotics or other drug residues. The researchers found clear connections between drug residues and the occurrence of certain infections. - First of all, we found that rats that wore an antidepressant called Citalopram had a three times higher risk of a kind of parasitic infection called capillaria. And then on the contrary, we found that rats with antibiotic substances in them had a 91 percent lower risk of a type of bacterial infection called leptospira, says Anna Jonsson Sundberg. Can affect the rats' behavior The researchers believe that the drug residues can also affect the rats' behavior and thus how infectious agents are spread between animals. - Since we saw an effect of antidepressants that increased the risk of infection by a parasite, you can guess that it might have something to do with the rats becoming more fearless, social, aggressive, that they interact more with other rats in a way that increases the spread of infection, she says. The findings raise questions about the consequences pharmaceutical contamination can have for both animals and humans. Since rats are known carriers of several diseases, changes in their behavior and infection patterns can have implications far beyond the environments in which the animals live. "The rat is perhaps the most dangerous" And although thoughts easily go to large predators that are affected by drugs, the researcher believes that the biggest threat may be much smaller than that. - If you have to think about which animal would be most dangerously affected by drugs, you might think of something big and aggressive. Gunnar managed to get out of the car, lock the doors and alert the police. The perpetrator was later sentenced to a few months of community service.

After the incident, Gunnar has had to process the experience on his own.

- I have not received any help. You have to manage it yourself. I've had some nightmares, he says. More choose to report Researchers believe that there are several possible reasons for the increase in reported assault crimes. An important explanation is that more people choose to report when they are exposed to violence. The healthcare system's new routines also mean that more cases are detected and reported.

Criminologist Linn Persson at Malmö University says that the statistics have changed.

- Ten years ago, it was mainly men who reported assault. Now we see that the difference between women and men is decreasing and that more women are reporting, she says.

She also says that the number of reported cases of abuse among children and young people under the age of 17 has increased.

- This indicates that more young people and more women are prepared to report when they are exposed to crime. We also know that young people today have a lower tolerance for violence and other crimes, says Linn Persson. Drive less taxis after the incident Even though Gunnar's bruises have healed, the incident still lingers in the memory. It has affected both his security and his work.

- I drive less taxis now than I did before, says Gunnar.

In connection with the large fires in Southern Europe, Anders Granström raises the risk of certain types of hedges.  - I have seen several pictures of hedges burning in residential areas and cities.  It is mainly about dense conifer hedges that are often used as privacy protection or demarcation between plots.  - They are flammable and are absolutely not the right material in gardens if you want to reduce the risk of fire. 04cd77f9d858dfea668637cc299945cc874ccda4: Place the food correctly in the fridge - avoid the traps of the rotten month
1eb712c205d7699623062cc7230b864354ffbd1b: During the rotting month, the risk of food spoiling quickly increases, especially when the heat and humidity rise. How you place the food in the refrigerator can be decisive for both durability and health. Professor Marie-Louise Danielsson Tham, expert in food hygiene, explains why the right placement in the fridge can save you from illness. Not all refrigerators are the same Modern refrigerators often have circulating cold air, which makes the temperature more even. In older refrigerators, the cold air sinks downwards and this can create a large temperature difference between the shelves. - Measure the temperature where it is coldest in the fridge. Sensitive foods should be kept where it is cold, often in the middle, says Marie-Louise Danielsson Tham. How to place different foods Dairy products, seafood and other sensitive food should be in the middle of the fridge, where the temperature is lowest. Vegetables and fruit, on the other hand, should be in the vegetable drawer at the bottom, where it is a little warmer and they are not at risk of freezing. - If you put fruit and vegetables too cold, they get sad quickly. They freeze, quite simply, says Danielsson Tham. The door compartment is the warmest part of the refrigerator and is best suited for products that are not so sensitive, such as ketchup, mayonnaise and some dressings. Milk and dairy products should not be left there, as they turn sour faster. - In the door compartments, you should have things that are not so sensitive, she says. Tips to avoid food waste Eggs keep best in the refrigerator and can be stored significantly longer than at room temperature. Tomatoes do best outside the fridge, while lemons can be kept in the vegetable drawer. - You don't want to throw away food unnecessarily, says Marie-Louise Danielsson Tham. Keeping an eye on the temperature of the refrigerator and placing the food correctly is especially important during the rotting month, when bacteria multiply faster in the heat. - Everyone should watch out, I think. You never know when the heat will come, says Danielsson Tham.

e16ecc1a1a4646b7b479e16ff9757b4a61d10e18: Thousands of migrants crossed the border from Morocco to the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Thursday. Spain sent military to the area to help the border police and the borders to Ceuta and Melilla were closed. According to the news agency Reuters, 49,000 people have crossed the border in one day. During Friday, there were reports that at least 18 people have died. According to the Spanish newspaper El País, they are believed to have drowned while trying to swim to Ceuta from Morocco. At the same time, police and border guards describe the situation as very strained. To El País, several police officers say that they are "one step away from operational collapse". More deaths According to Rachid Sbihi from the civil guard trade union AUGC, more than 25 dead migrants have been found in recent days. According to the newspaper, many migrants have tried to get to Ceuta following a decision by Spain's Supreme Court earlier in July. The court ruled that migrants stopped at sea outside Ceuta and Melilla cannot be turned away outright. At the same time, the local newspaper Ceuta Actualidad reports that a Whatsapp group with over 800 members has been started. In 2023, a civil court sentenced Trump to pay SEK 56 million in damages for sexual assault and defamation. On July 14 of this year, it was stated that that sum had been paid.  New judgment in 2024 In 2024, Trump was convicted again of defamation against Carroll for comments made in 2019. According to the lawsuit, Trump claimed that the accusations were made up. Among other things, he is said to have said that Carroll is "not his type" and that the accusation was made up to increase sales of her book. He was sentenced to pay approximately SEK 807 million in damages.  Claiming immunity President Trump's lawyers are now asking the Supreme Court to overturn the 2024 ruling. At the time of the comments, Trump was president, and the lawyers thus argue that the statements were part of his official duties and therefore protected by presidential immunity.

They also refer to the Westfall Act, a federal law that protects government employees from certain lawsuits related to the performance of their duties. They argue that Trump should be able to change his name as a defendant in the case against the US state. In practice, that could stop the process, as the US government cannot be sued for defamation.

d28f1487c8960df9b8bd9e31f77d0d8541299313: The 1,500 cargo ships stuck in the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the US-Iran war could be the starting point for a marine ecological disaster, a new study warns. It is not unusual for cargo ships to bring microbes and algae from one port to another. But when the ships have been stationary for as long as many have done in the Strait of Hormuz, the risk increases that, for example, algae or invertebrates such as centipedes will get stuck and accompany them to the ship's final destination. Centipedes are a form of crustaceans that often get stuck on, for example, ships - longnecks and barnacles are two that occur in Swedish waters, but there are thousands of species, some of which are parasites. Intruder The researchers see the situation as potentially very serious. When you move organisms around, they can reduce the biodiversity of the regions where they invade and cause local extinction of organisms, the study's lead author Mario Tamburri told The Guardian. The researchers emphasize that the human suffering in and around the Strait of Hormuz is probably the most urgent thing for the outside world to care about, but that one also needs to think about the risk that the stationary ships can pose. In many ways, it's like tracking the flu or covid. You want to be prepared for it, detect it early. If you find it, you want to be able to act immediately, says Tamburri to The Guardian. Spread The researchers are concerned that the ships could mean a "super spreader event", especially for ports in countries similar to the Persian Gulf in temperature, such as India and Singapore. The region in the Middle East has long been known to have dozens of invasive species that have hitched a ride on international merchant ships, species that do well in the region's harsh environment. It is the tough organisms that can often withstand these extreme environments that become really good invaders, says Tamburri to The Guardian.

The cloud is believed to reach its largest size approximately 90 seconds after impact and may extend several miles above the lunar surface. The researchers emphasize at the same time that it is not at all certain that it will be possible to see from Earth. The cloud is expected to be significantly weaker than the bright light of the moon and the observations are also affected by weather and visibility. Points to future problems The researchers hope that the crash will provide answers to how dust and rock are dispersed when something hits the surface of the moon at high speed. Wired writes that the knowledge could become important when both the US and China plan new manned missions and future bases on the moon. Material ejected from the surface can, in the worst case, damage equipment or astronauts. - We will apparently colonize the moon quite soon, says William Jo at the University of Texas to the site. It is a package of laws, guidelines and approaches that, among other things, should make it easier for individuals to understand if they are interacting with an AI service. The package, the first substantial one of its kind, is however large and tight, which has meant that the EU does not intend to pull out the penalty stick and start swinging right away. Different parts of the package will be implemented at different dates. One part, which, among other things, concerns the marking of whether someone interacts with an AI service, comes into force now. Other parts, such as potentially hefty fines for companies that deal with "high-risk AI" and don't behave, are postponed until 2027. Political gamble The EU's view on AI is a sensitive issue, with critics saying that a cautious stance risks leaving the Union on the platform as the train towards the future moves. The political tariff war between US President Donald Trump and the EU is partly built on Trump's anger that the EU has fined American tech companies that the EU does not think have followed the Union's rules. Supporters of the EU's more cautious AI stance often highlight individual high-profile incidents where AI "lost control" as evidence that tougher rules are good. A couple of days ago they got water to their mill when a so-called AI agent, an autonomous AI program, "escaped" onto the internet when Open AI (Chat GPT) tested it in a local environment without access to the public network. Voluntariness and fines Parts of the AI ​​act are based on voluntariness and a "code of conduct", where many of the world's largest tech companies have already said they intend to follow the guidelines - including Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Open AI and Anthropic. However, Elon Musk's X has only agreed to the security part of the "code" and Meta (Facebook and Instagram) has so far not signed at all. Exactly how effective the EU regulatory package will be remains to be seen. d75f26e68467fd9d3213a24c98fc1e18da65bb75: The price drop for apartments in particular stands out in the monthly figures from state-run SBAB and the housing site Booli, and was greater than the price drop for houses. Apartment prices fell by 4.6 percent in July for Sweden as a whole, while house prices fell by 1.4 percent. The prices of apartments in Greater Stockholm fell the most, where they plummeted by as much as 7.1 percent. Robert Boije, chief economist at SBAB, is surprised himself and has no explanation for what is driving the price drop. The price drop in Greater Stockholm really stands out, he says, but states that the price drop cannot be explained by a drop in the price of apartments in the central parts of Stockholm, but affects the county as a whole. Higher than usual in the summer Housing prices tend to moderate during the summer months when people are on holiday and taking it easy and the turnover of housing is lower. But that has been taken into account in the index, according to Boije. The price drop for apartments is significantly greater than it usually is during the summer, he says, and also refutes macroeconomic explanations. In that case, we would have seen an equally large price race for villas. Normalization Despite the price drop in July, Stockholm, together with Malmö, belongs to the region where housing prices have fallen at least since the spring of 2022, when they fell after a long period of rise. One could therefore speak of a certain normalization from the high housing prices in 2022, reasons Boije, who however does not want to draw any conclusions until the August figures come. It is then when many people start working and studying and change homes that prices jump up, and then stabilize again, he says.
